title: income-rate was measured on spendable cash only, so the savings model never released
description:
Introduced 2026-09-08 with the savings model; found the same evening from game 89.

sampleIncome (rules/engine.go) sampled:

    cash := env.State.Player.Cash

while every rule spends from RuleEnv.Cash():

    return e.State.Player.Cash + e.State.Player.Resources

Player.Cash is the spendable half. Ore waiting in the silos sits in Player.Resources. Spendable cash hovers near zero, so its 500-tick delta hovers near zero and is essentially never positive.

Consequence: `income-rate > 0`, the release clause the savings model in affordable() depends on, was unreachable by construction. Measured over game 89s 149 exported states, income-rate was positive in 0% of them. The savings clauses were therefore permanently armed, and they removed 36 of the 43 percentage points of states in which a base defence was affordable — leaving about 7%.

Game 89 (germany vs russia, the same matchup as the 88 win): build-base-defense acted TWICE, first at tick 8571. The attack landed at 10881. Construction yard lost at 11211, war factory at 12151, game over at 12741 having run 40960 the game before.

Measuring the deltas on cash+resources instead, they are positive in 20% of the sampled states, so the release would have fired regularly.

Fixed: sampleIncome now sums both, with a test asserting that ore arriving in the silos counts as income and that IncomeRate() agrees with what sampleIncome stored.

Two lessons worth keeping:
  1. A derived metric must be measured on the same quantity the consumers act on. Two different notions of "cash" in one system, and the rule layer and the sampler picked different ones.
  2. The savings model was designed to be self-limiting — hold, income accrues, hold releases. A release that can never fire turns a self-limiting design into an unconditional one, and nothing in the tests or the replay would have caught it: the clause was correct, the measurement was not.

title: Sidecar does not re-engage after a game restart: handshake completes, then no state is ever processed
description:
Game 89 (2026-09-08 22:02): the previous match ended, OpenRA reconnected, and the sidecar went silent.

Log after the new game began — one line, total:

  22:02:22.485  connection read ended  error="read length: EOF"   (x2, old game)
  22:02:22.655  new connection accepted                            (x2)
  22:02:22.864  player identified  faction=england opponents=[ukraine]
  22:02:22.864  terrain grid set
  22:02:22.864  strategist started
  ... nothing, for 11.5 minutes and counting

State of the world while stalled:
  - sidecar process alive, STAT S+, 1.8% CPU, not crashed
  - OpenRA alive (pid 4668) and CONNECTED: 3 endpoints on /tmp/vimy.sock, 8 socket FDs held
  - HTTP dashboard on :8080 answers 200, but renders the PREVIOUS games tick ranges
  - no doctrine generated, no rule set swapped, no diagnostics of any kind

The diagnostic that localises it: military diagnostics / production diagnostics log on EVERY evaluation and are driven by incoming game state, independently of the strategist. Zero of them means state messages are not being processed at all. So this is not a slow LLM call on the strategist path — the read/evaluate path itself is stalled after reconnect.

Handshake messages (hello -> player identified, terrain grid set) DID arrive on the new connection, so the socket and the first reads work. Something after the handshake does not resume.

Suspects, unverified:
  - a goroutine from the old connection still holding engine state (memMu / mu) so Evaluate blocks forever
  - the new connection handler writing to a channel whose reader belonged to the old game
  - two connections accepted per game, and the reader attached to the wrong one

Why it matters beyond one lost game: a silent stall is indistinguishable from bad play. We spent ten minutes reading the previous games final unit counts as though they were live, and concluded the AI had a big economy and no army. Any back-to-back game session may have been affected.

Fixes worth considering together:
  1. Find and fix the stall (needs a goroutine dump — see 3).
  2. A watchdog: if no game state has been processed for N seconds while a connection is open, log loudly at ERROR. Silence should never be the failure mode.
  3. Expose net/http/pprof on the dashboard port so a live hang can be diagnosed without killing the process. There is no pprof today and that is why this issue has suspects rather than a cause.
  4. Reset per-game state on connection teardown, and assert it is clean on accept.

title: Vehicle branch arrives past halftime: war factory at 57% of the game, first tank at 72%
description:
Currie's new onset timeline, game 83 (24020 ticks):

   4-23%  entire base: barracks, radar, power, refineries, AIRFIELD
  30-34%  squads form
     55%  first scouting of any kind
     57%  build-war-factory — first and only action
     61%  first squad-attack
  68-69%  scout vehicle produced, first patrol
     72%  produce-vehicle — the first ground vehicle of the game
  74-83%  reactive rules only (retreat, flee, emergency defence)

The war factory not existing until 57% is the root of several things filed separately today:

- produce-scout-vehicle requires has-role(war-factory), so it could not fire before 57% regardless of priority. vimy-dtg blamed the scouting rules; the building was the constraint.
- vehicle_weight was 0.35 all game and the first vehicle came at 72%.
- The doctrine's plan was air dominance PLUS ground rockets for SEAD. The airfield went up at 22%, the war factory at 57%: the air half executed and the ground half had no factory to come from.

Every rule involved 'worked' — build-war-factory is matched 1 / acted 1. This is invisible to blame analysis and was only found once onset timing was rendered.

Investigate the build-order priorities: what outranks build-war-factory for the first half of a game whose doctrine wants vehicles?

title: Nothing scouts for the first half of the game: both scouting paths need mid-game assets
description:
Game 83 (loss, 234 states). Full chain:

1. produce-vehicle has priority 480; produce-scout-vehicle has 465. The category is 'produce-vehicle exclusive', so only the highest-priority matching rule fires per tick. vehicle_weight was 0.35 all game, so produce-vehicle was live essentially always. The scout is therefore never built — not rarely, never.

2. scout-with-scouts requires count(idle-scouts) > 0: 228 blocked / 228 SOLE out of 234 states. It is the single most solely-blocked clause of any real rule in the game, and it is blocked because step 1 means no scout unit has ever existed.

3. The fallback, scout-with-idle-units, requires count(unassigned-idle-ground) >= ground-attack-group-size — a FULL attack group (6) of spare idle ground units before it will send one to look around. 228 blocked / 130 sole. The same pool is drained by harvester-guard, ground-defense and ground-attack, so it is essentially never met.

4. Result: enemy base not discovered until tick 17190, roughly 11 minutes into a 16-minute game.

5. squad-attack's dominant blocker is then 'exists best-ground-target or exists nearest-enemy' at 130 blocked / 59 sole — the largest single cause of the attack squad not attacking. It had 6/6 units and nowhere to go.

Two fixes, both cheap:
- Raise produce-scout-vehicle above produce-vehicle while has-enemy-intel() is false (it already requires 'not has-enemy-intel()', so the boost self-cancels once a base is found). This is the deliberate-tie-breaking work applied to an exclusive category.
- Lower scout-with-idle-units' bar from ground-attack-group-size to 1-2. Scouting is what a spare unit does early, not something that waits for an entire army to be idle.
notes:
CORRECTION — the mechanism in the original description is WRONG. Retracting it:

FALSE: 'produce-scout-vehicle always loses the exclusive produce-vehicle category', 'the scout is never built', 'scout-with-scouts blocked because no scout unit ever existed'.

The engine's matched/acted counters for game 83 say otherwise:
  produce-scout-vehicle   matched 1  acted 1
  scout-with-scouts       matched 3  acted 3
  scout-with-idle-units   matched 7  acted 7
  produce-vehicle         matched 3  acted 3
Currie's headline Preempted count is 0 — no rule lost its exclusive category except produce-spy (2). produce-scout-vehicle does not appear in the report at all, because the dead-rule list only holds rules that never fired, and it fired.

I read the priority numbers (produce-vehicle 480 > produce-scout-vehicle 465) into Currie's 228-sole figures and asserted a cause. Those sole counts are a claim about the SAMPLE (every 15th evaluation), not the game — the documented trap from 2026-09-07, walked into again.

TRUE, from first_tick/last_tick (game ran to tick 24020):
  13250  first scouting of any kind (scout-with-idle-units)   55% through
  16370  first scout vehicle produced                         68%
  16690  first scout patrol                                   70%
  17190  enemy base discovered                                72%

Nothing scouted for 13,250 ticks with scout_priority at 0.80 throughout. Both paths depend on mid-game assets:
  - produce-scout-vehicle requires has-role(war-factory)
  - scout-with-idle-units requires count(unassigned-idle-ground) >= ground-attack-group-size (6)

There is no early-game scouting mechanism. The fallback's bar of 6 is the fixable half: unassigned-idle-ground includes infantry, so a bar of 1-2 would let the first rifleman scout instead of waiting for six spare units that the harvester-guard / ground-defense / ground-attack squads keep consuming.

Downstream cost is real: squad-attack's largest single blocker is 'exists best-ground-target or exists nearest-enemy' at 130 blocked / 59 sole, and squad-attack managed matched 3 / acted 2 in a game where it had a full 6/6 squad for the last four minutes.

title: Building rules ignore the cash reserves, so defenses starve the radar
description:
Reserves are respected by unit production only, so building rules outspend them.

Observed across games 71 and 72, same doctrine string, both with the vimy-tex
radar reserve in place.

Game 72 build activity, by diagnostic samples of currentItem:

    proc 36   tsla 33   dome 17   powr 15   weap 12   e1 8   ftur 7

Thirty-three samples of tesla coil. At groundDefense 0.75 the compiled rule is

    build-base-defense   priority 550   category defense (exclusive)
    ... RoleCount(pillbox|camo_pillbox|turret|flame_tower|tesla_coil) < 8
    ... && Cash() >= 600

Eight defenses at up to 1500 each is 12,000 credits, gated at a 600 floor. Against
that, build-radar sits at priority 570 in category `economy` needing Cash() >= 1000.
Different categories, so exclusivity cannot arbitrate — both fire in the same tick
and race for the same cash. The rule with the LOWER floor wins that race every
time, so defenses are built and the radar is not.

Game 71: radar at tick 7,260, two combat vehicles in 27,570 ticks.
Game 72: no radar by tick 9,000; Vehicle queue still harv,apc,truk,ftrk.

Cash on hand was 0 from tick 3,500 in both games, BEFORE any harvester trouble
started (flee-harvesters first fired at 8,900 in game 71). So this is a separate
defect from vimy-mfq, not a symptom of it. vimy-mfq was real and is fixed —
resources now flow, 445/425/382/834 across game 72 where game 71 was flat zero —
but the cash is spent as fast as it arrives.

Root cause
----------
buildCashCondition / the `reserves` defs are used ONLY by produce-* rules. Every
building rule has a bare cash gate: build-base-defense at 600, build-radar at
1000, build-tech-center at 1500. So the reserve added in vimy-tex protects the
radar from infantry and flak trucks, and not at all from defenses.

That is the same failure vimy-tex fixed, one layer up: a cash race with no
reservation, where the cheapest rule wins and the tech gate starves.

Fix
---
Give the building rules the same reserve discipline the unit rules have — at
minimum, build-base-defense and build-aa-defense should hold above the radar
reserve while the doctrine wants vehicles and radar is missing:

    require has-role(radar) or vehicle-weight <= 0.1 or cash >= 600 + 1000

Consider whether the reserve belongs in one place rather than being applied rule
by rule. Every rule that spends should respect it; today the set that does is
whichever ones happened to call buildCashCondition.

Note the interaction: a defense-heavy doctrine (groundDefense 0.75, which is what
the LLM chose in response to being raided) is exactly the one that can never
tech out of being raided. The doctrine asks for a fortified perimeter AND medium
and heavy tanks, and gets only the perimeter.

Port note: this is a rule change and would land in doctrine.vy as well as the Go
compiler.
notes:
PARTIAL FIX 2026-09-08: one savings model, applied to the three rules this issue names.

affordable() in buildings.vy now reads:

  cash >= cost
  and (vehicle-weight <= 0.1 or has-role(radar) or cash >= cost + 1000)
  and (income-rate > 0 or has-role(refinery)      or cash >= cost + 1400)
  and (income-rate > 0 or has-role(war-factory)   or vehicle-weight <= 0.1 or cash >= cost + war-factory-cash())
  and (income-rate > 0 or has-role(service-depot) or vehicle-weight <= 0.3 or cash >= cost + service-depot-cash())
  and (income-rate > 0 or has-role(radar)         or tech-priority <= 0.2  or cash >= cost + 1000)

Two properties worth recording:

- Separate conjuncts, so the effect is the MAX of the reserves and never the sum. A doctrine wanting vehicles and tech at once is not charged for both. This is what went wrong on 2026-09-07 when a reserve change stacked to +4500 and priced the AI out of its own units.
- income-rate > 0 releases every clause, and it is NET cash. Negative or zero means every credit is being committed as it arrives, which is when saving matters. Once a balance accumulates the restriction lifts, so the model is self-limiting: hold, income accrues, hold releases. That is the deadlock guard.

Applied only via affordable(), which feeds exactly build-base-defense, build-aa-defense and build-gap-generator — the defense rules this issue names as starving the radar. reserves() (core.vy) and scaled-reserves() (production.vy) still exist and still overlap; consolidating all three is the remaining work.

A design constraint found on the way: select() is specialised when the doctrine lands, so it cannot branch on runtime state like has-role. A savings model cannot compute a NUMBER from the current game; it can only be written as boolean conjuncts. That is why this is a conjunction and not the next-gate-cost() function originally sketched.

title: The economy is capped at four refineries, and Vimy sits against that cap most of every game
description:
User asked to look at the economy after three straight games of armour 5 / refinery 4 / cash 350.

build-extra-refinery caps refineries at 'role-count(refinery) < lerp(1, 5, economy-priority)'. The strategist picks economy_priority 0.80 consistently, so the cap is 4. At economy_priority 1.0 it is still only 5. produce-extra-harvester then pins harvesters to 'role-count(refinery) + 2'.

Measured against the cap the doctrine actually chose:
  game 105 (win)  cap 4, peak 4, AT CAP 65% of sampled states, harvesters 6
  game 107        cap 4, peak 5, AT CAP 89%, harvesters 7
  game 108        cap 4, peak 4, AT CAP 61%, harvesters 6

So this is not a soft ceiling Vimy occasionally brushes; it is the binding constraint for most of every game.

This is the same defect vimy-ogl fixed for units — a standing-count ceiling low enough that the rule, not the game, decides the size of the thing — and that fix deliberately covered production caps only. The economy caps were not touched, and they sit one layer upstream of everything fixed today:

  refineries capped at 4 -> cash median ~350 -> 'cash >= 800' holds ~12% of post-war-factory states -> 4-5 live combat vehicles.

Every armour change today (vimy-2kx depot savings, vimy-ogl caps, vimy-tbe infantry hold) ran into this wall. Armour has been 5 in games 106, 107 and 108 regardless.

Also worth noting build-extra-refinery requires 'lerp(1, 5, economy-priority) > 2', i.e. economy_priority above roughly 0.4, before it will build a third refinery at all.

Fix direction, deliberately not chosen yet: raise the top of the lerp the way vimy-ogl raised the unit tops, leaving the bottom alone so economy-light doctrines are unaffected. Whether harvesters should stay tied to refineries + 2 is a separate question — more harvesters per refinery is a real strategy, and the current formula forbids it.

Caution: unlike the unit caps, more refineries means more buildings to defend, and games 98-100 were decided by economic raiding. A bigger, thinner economy against ukraine or germany — where Vimy is 0 for 53 — could be worse, not better. This wants measuring, not assuming.

title: Repair never runs: the cash floor reads the banked half, not the money the rules spend
description:
User observation, game 107: 'I am seeing no repairs happening to vimy's base' — damaged and burning buildings, including a refinery on a yellow health bar, with nothing repairing.

repair-buildings has shown 0 acted in every game this session. One doctrine window in game 106 had it at 81 matched / 0 acted. The rule is trivially permissive — 'require count(damaged-buildings) > 0' — so every decision lives in the action, which is why the counters look busy and nothing happens.

ActionRepairDamagedBuildings (actions.go:1006) opens with:
    const repairCashFloor = 500
    if env.State.Player.Cash < repairCashFloor { return nil }

That reads Player.Cash, the BANKED half. RuleEnv.Cash() — what 'cash' means everywhere else in the rule layer — is Player.Cash + Player.Resources (env.go:106). These are the only two places in the action layer that read Player.Cash bare; the second is the repair_budget_ratio headroom check at actions.go:1023.

Vimy's COMBINED cash median has been 350-400 across games 102-106, so the banked half alone is smaller still, and a floor of 500 measured against it is effectively unreachable. Repair has been a complete no-op.

Same class as vimy-9w5, where income-rate was sampled on Player.Cash while the rules spent Player.Cash + Resources.

Fix: use env.Cash() in both places. Then revisit the 500 floor and repairMaxConcurrent (2), because they have never actually been exercised — the floor was chosen to stop repair pinning cash at zero, and that reasoning was sound but was being applied to the wrong quantity. Expect repair to start consuming income once this lands, which is the behaviour the floor exists to bound, so the two changes should be measured together.

Also unexercised and worth a look once repair runs: the underPressure filter skips non-critical buildings while is-rushed or harvester-harassed, which covers a lot of a typical game.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Nathan Stehr
comments.text: db031f3 — repair now reads env.Cash() (Player.Cash + Resources) instead of Player.Cash at both gates. The 500 floor is kept: against the right quantity it passes in 28-43% of states across games 104, 105 and 107, which is the 'repair when something is spare' gate it was meant to be. TestRepairSpendsAgainstTotalCash verifies it and was checked against the old field, where it fails. Two gates that have never run will now be exercised for the first time: repairMaxConcurrent (2) and the underPressure filter that skips non-critical buildings while rushed or harassed — worth watching whether repair starts eating income, which is the failure the floor exists to prevent.

title: Squad hunts a stale base centroid instead of the enemy building it can see
description:
User observation, game 105 endgame: 'there is one enemy building left, vimy has effectively won. But the squad is wandering around and not finishing it off' — then, minutes later, 'finally, Vimy did finish it off'. It cost real time in a game Vimy went on to WIN, so next time it could cost the win.

Mechanism:

NearestEnemyBase() (env.go:1779) reads ONLY getEnemyBases(e.Memory) — the remembered intel centroid. It never consults e.State.Enemies, i.e. buildings Vimy can currently see.

SquadAttackKnownBase (actions.go:2532) targets that centroid, and when the squad arrives to find nothing it runs a 16-step hunt around it:
  baseRadius := mapDim / 16                 (~8 on a 128 map)
  scale := 0.25 + aggression*1.25           (0.56 at aggression 0.25)
  radius := baseRadius * scale              (~4 cells)
So once a base is razed down to one outlying building, the squad circles a ~4-cell radius of empty ground where the base used to be.

Why it eventually resolved: squad-attack and squad-attack-known-base share the exclusive category ground-attack-choice. At aggression 0.25, squad-attack is attack-priority() = 250 and squad-attack-known-base is attack-priority() - 10 = 240, so squad-attack OUTRANKS it and would have killed the building at once — but it requires 'exists best-ground-target or exists nearest-enemy', and while the squad milled around empty ground it could see nothing. The hunt eventually wandered it into visual range, squad-attack then fired, and the building died. That is the 'finally'.

Fix: InferredEnemyBaseCenter() (env.go:1709) already exists and already weights currently-visible buildings above the persisted centroid — its own doc says it 'lets siege and rally rules aim at a base seen only in fragments'. SquadAttackKnownBase should prefer it over NearestEnemyBase, or NearestEnemyBase should consult visible buildings first.

Do NOT change NearestEnemyBase globally without checking callers — ActionScoutPatrol's targetKnownBase uses it too, and that path was just retuned in vimy-xhz.

Secondary: the hunt radius is tiny. Even aimed correctly, ~4 cells is a small search for a razed base. Consider widening it as steps are exhausted.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Nathan Stehr
comments.text:
Fixed the search, not the aiming.

Investigated the obvious fix first and rejected it: individual enemy BUILDING positions are not remembered anywhere — getEnemyBases stores one averaged centroid per owner — and InferredEnemyBaseCenter weights that centroid at 5.0 against 3.0 for currently-visible buildings, so it would still average onto empty ground between a dead base site and a surviving outlier. Aiming better is not available with this data model. In game 105 the squad also had no vision on the barracks (it was across the map), so 'target the visible building' would not have fired either.

What was actually broken: huntOffset walks 8 compass points at radius R (steps 1-8) and 8 at 2R (steps 9-16), and the caller wrapped Step back to 1 at 16. R = mapDim/16 * (0.25 + aggression*1.25) = 4 cells at aggression 0.25, so the entire reachable search was 8 cells around a point the enemy had abandoned, on a 128-cell map. Two rings, forever.

Fix: extracted huntMaxStep(mapDim, radius), which grows the ring count until the search spans half the map (ceiling division — truncating left the outer ring short). At aggression 0.25 that is 16 rings / 64 cells, at 0.8 it is 7 rings / 70 cells. Previously 8 and 20.

Safe to widen because squad-attack (attack-priority()) outranks squad-attack-known-base (attack-priority() - 10 below aggression 0.6) in the shared exclusive category ground-attack-choice, and only needs a visible target. So a growing search runs only while nothing is in sight, and finding something hands over. That is how game 105 resolved on its own — the hunt blundered into visual range.

Test added: TestHuntReachesAcrossTheMap, asserting the hunt reaches at least half the map at both cautious and aggressive settings. It caught a truncation bug — the aggressive case reached 60 of the 64 required cells.

go test and cargo test both exit 0. Committed 1cde161.

title: Scouts are abandoned at map waypoints, and squads form with no regard to where units are
description:
User observation, game 105 early (minimap): 'Scouting was good but for multiple ticks the infantry seemed paused in the corners and center of the map.'

Chain, all confirmed in code:

1. scout-with-idle-units (micro.vy) AttackMoves up to 2 idle GROUND COMBAT units to perimeter waypoints. ActionScoutWithIdleUnits (actions.go:1072) rotates a unit to the next waypoint only when the rule FIRES AGAIN.

2. The rule's guards are 'require not enemies-visible' and 'require not has-enemy-intel()'. Both flip on first contact, so the rule stops firing early and permanently — and the units it dispatched are left standing on whatever waypoint they last received. That is the pause the user saw.

3. Nothing recalls them. recall-overextended exists only for squads (recall-overextended-ground-attack / -naval-attack in micro.vy); there is no equivalent for loose units.

4. FormSquad (actions.go:2305) fills a squad from env.UnassignedIdleGround() by taking pool[i] in iteration order, with NO proximity sort. A squad can therefore be assembled from units standing in opposite corners of the map.

5. That squad then converges on its target piecemeal rather than as a body.

Why this matters beyond the cosmetic: attrition has held at roughly 4:1 through every change this session (game 103: 36 vehicle orders for peak 10 alive, 92 infantry for peak 19; game 104: 170 infantry for peak 38). Production, caps and timing have all been fixed without moving it. Units arriving at a fight one at a time is a mechanism that would produce exactly that, and it also matches an earlier user observation from a previous session — a minimap where 'we should know where the base is, but the units are spread out moving'.

Possible fixes, not yet chosen:
(a) Sort the FormSquad pool by distance from base (or from the squad's rally point) so a squad is built from units that are actually together. Smallest change, likely the biggest effect on cohesion.
(b) Give scout-with-idle-units a release: when its guards flip, clear the idleScoutMoveSent assignments so the units are plainly unassigned, or issue a move home.
(c) Let the scouting rule keep firing after contact so dispatched units continue rotating rather than freezing, with a separate cap on how many units may be out.

(a) and (b) are complementary: (a) stops scattered squads forming, (b) stops units being stranded in the first place.

Not implemented — game 105 is measuring vimy-tbe and a second change would confound it.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Nathan Stehr
comments.text:
Half fixed (56004d0): the scout party is now sticky.

ActionScoutWithIdleUnits took the first two units from IdleGroundUnits(), which lists in State.Units order, so a newly built rifle could arrive ahead of a scout and take its place. Since a scout only advances to its next waypoint when this action runs FOR IT, the displaced unit was never advanced again and stood on its last waypoint for the rest of the game. Units already carrying an assignment are now picked first, and fresh ones only fill the remainder.

TestScoutWithIdleUnitsKeepsTheSameParty verifies it, and was checked against the pre-fix code: the party grew from 2 to 4 units in a single extra firing, which is the stranding mechanism directly.

STILL OPEN, and this is the larger half:
- The rule itself stops firing on first contact ('require not enemies-visible', 'require not has-enemy-intel()'), so whichever two units are out at that moment stay out permanently. Nothing recalls loose units — recall-overextended is squad-only. Fixing this needs a RULE (a recall for idle unassigned units far from base), which lands mid-game at the next doctrine compile, so it was deferred while game 107 runs.
- Units stranded before the party stabilises are still stranded.

WITHDRAWN from this issue: the claim that FormSquad's lack of proximity sorting is a meaningful attrition cause. It is true that FormSquad takes pool[i] in iteration order with no distance sort, but the user then watched two separate cohesive squads attack and withdraw as a body, including one combined-arms push with infantry, tanks and artillery shelling a war factory from stand-off. Scattered squads look like the exception rather than the rule, so the ~4:1 attrition needs a different explanation. Worth revisiting only if squads are actually observed arriving piecemeal.

comments.author: Nathan Stehr
comments.text: 723b195 — recall-stray-units added. Walks unassigned idle ground units back to the base centroid once has-enemy-intel() holds, which is the same moment scouting stops being worth doing. Threshold 35% of the map diagonal against the 20% that counts as 'at home', so a unit just outside the perimeter is not shuttled back and forth; the designated scout is exempt. No new DSL collection was needed — the distance test lives in the action and the rule reuses unassigned-idle-ground. Required registering the action name in vimyc (src/env.rs) and adding the rule to POST_PORT, since it postdates the frozen corpus. With 56004d0 bounding how many units can be stranded, this collects the ones already out. Closes the half of this issue that was left open; the FormSquad proximity claim stays withdrawn.

title: Infantry outbids armour: the vehicle savings hold releases after a single tank
description:
User observation after game 104: 'Lots of infantry produced and big squads but didn't see the same for tanks and artillery' — under a doctrine with vehicle_weight 0.60 and preferred_vehicle starting medium_tank.

Game 104: produce-infantry acted 170, produce-vehicle 26, peak e1 38, peak armour 8. matched == acted for both, so produce-vehicle was blocked at the condition level, not losing a race in the action.

Replaying produce-vehicle's conditions over the 616 sampled states that had a war factory:
  cash >= 800               holds  13%   (sole blocker in 218 states)
  not queue-busy(Vehicle)   holds  39%   (sole blocker in 63)
  combat-veh-count < 25     holds 100%   <- the cap is NOT binding any more
So cash is the constraint, and the cap change from vimy-ogl did its job.

Mechanism: infantry-reserves' FIRST clause holds a full tank's worth (cost + 800) in reserve, but escapes on 'role-count(light|medium|heavy|artillery) >= 1'. One tank and the protection is off permanently; only the third clause remains, worth 800 * (vehicle-weight - infantry-weight) = 800 * 0.35 = 280. So infantry cleared at 380 and a tank at 800, and every time cash crossed 380 a rifle was bought. 170 rifles is ~17000 credits, which is 20 medium tanks of spending.

The escape was written when the goal was 'get at least one tank', which was correct while the medium-tank cap WAS one tank. It is the wrong goal now that accumulation is possible — same shape as vimy-2kx, a savings clause that exists but stops biting when it matters.

Fix: escape on a half-strength vehicle target instead of a single tank.
  or combat-vehicle-count >= army-cap(2.0, 9.0, vehicle-weight)

title: Vimy cannot accumulate an army: production caps are standing-army ceilings, and multiplicative gates collapse them
description:
User observation from game 103 (screenshot of the russia base): the built-in AI is an ACCUMULATOR — it grows a base and a standing force without limit, and once it reaches critical mass Vimy loses regardless of doctrine. Vimy should not have to accumulate for every doctrine (harassment is a legitimate shape) but it must be ABLE to.

Vimy is structurally forbidden from accumulating. Every produce-* rule carries a standing-army cap. At game 103's own doctrine (vehicle_weight 0.65, tech_priority 0.35, infantry_weight 0.20):
  produce-vehicle        combat-vehicle-count < lerp(3,10,vehicle-weight)                  = < 7.5  -> max 7
  produce-heavy-vehicle  medium+heavy < lerp(1,5, tech-priority * vehicle-weight)          = < 1.9  -> max 1
  produce-infantry       e1 < lerp(8,20,infantry-weight)                                    = < 10.4

Two distinct defects:

1. MULTIPLICATIVE GATES. tech-priority * vehicle-weight = 0.35 * 0.65 = 0.23, so an explicitly armoured doctrine lands at the BOTTOM of the cap range: one medium tank. This is why peak medium tanks was 1 in games 98,100,101,102 and 2 in 99. Game 103 reached 3 only because the generic produce-vehicle rule also builds medium tanks, bypassing the dedicated rule's cap. Same a*b pattern in produce-rocket-soldier (tech-priority * infantry-weight) and produce-attack-aircraft (tech-priority * air-weight). Two factors each <= 1 multiply to something smaller than either, so raising EITHER weight barely moves the cap.

2. CEILINGS, NOT BUDGETS. The caps say 'never HAVE more than N', not 'do not spend more than N on this'. With the ~4:1 attrition measured in game 103 (36 vehicle orders -> peak 10 alive; 92 infantry -> peak 19), a ceiling of 7 means Vimy hovers at 2-3 and can never bank a force. This is also why the directive's 'do not attack until you have a real force' never triggers: form-ground-attack needs 6 unassigned idle ground units and the ceiling keeps the pool below that.

vehicle_weight is a MIX weight (what fraction of my army is vehicles) being overloaded as a CEILING (how many may I have). There is no doctrine param for force size — see the param list in the .vy files; none of the 27 expresses it.

Note doctrine.baml:316 already instructs the strategist that failing to 'accumulate enough of either to win an engagement' is the known failure mode. The prompt asks for accumulation; the rule layer forbids it.

Options:
(a) Replace the multiplicative gates with max() or with the single relevant weight. Cheapest, directly fixes the 'one medium tank' pathology.
(b) Raise the top of the lerp ranges so a committed doctrine can field a real army (e.g. produce-vehicle lerp(3,10,..) -> lerp(3,20,..)). The bottom of each range should stay put so harassment doctrines are unaffected.
(c) Add a force-size doctrine param (BAML field + .vy param) so the strategist chooses the ceiling explicitly, defaulting to today's numbers. This is the real answer and matches the user's framing that accumulation should be a per-doctrine choice, but it is the largest change: new BAML field, make generate, plumb through vimyc params, RETUNED entries.

Recommend (a)+(b) first as a cheap testable pair, then (c).

comments.author: Nathan Stehr
comments.text:
Implemented (a), (b) and (c) together.

(a) MULTIPLICATIVE GATES REMOVED. Every 'tech-priority * <weight>' cap now uses max() of the two. At game 103's own doctrine (tech 0.35, vehicle 0.65) the medium+heavy cap goes from 1 to 5 — verified by compiling the real params through vimyc. Fixed in produce-heavy-vehicle, produce-rocket-soldier, produce-attack-aircraft and produce-advanced-ship (naval had the same defect).

(b) CAP TOPS RAISED, BOTTOMS LEFT ALONE so harassment doctrines are unaffected: vehicle 10->18, medium/heavy 5->8, infantry 20->30, rocket-soldier 8->10, aircraft 8->10, attack-aircraft 4->6, siege 8->12 / 3->5, specialist 6->8, naval 8->10 / 3->5.

(c) NEW force_size DOCTRINE PARAM. Follows the codebase's existing '0 = disabled -> current behaviour' idiom (commit_ratio, repair_budget_ratio, scout_reach_priority). Added to doctrine.baml with a description that draws the mix-vs-size distinction explicitly and tells the strategist the built-in AI accumulates without limit. Wired: Doctrine.ForceSize (json force_size) -> DoctrineParams picks it up from the tag automatically -> param force-size in core.vy. Also clamped in Validate() and mapped in strategist.go.

All 14 caps now route through one helper in core.vy:
  def force-scale() = select(force-size > 0.0, lerpf(1.0, 2.5, force-size), 1.0)
  def army-cap(low: float, high: float, weight: float) = trunc(lerpf(low, high, weight) * force-scale())
Multi-parameter defs were untested in this codebase (no existing def takes more than one) — verified by compiling a scratch rule set before committing to the shape.

Verified by compiling the real game-103 params: force-size 0.0 -> vehicle cap 12, infantry 12, siege 3, medium+heavy 5. force-size 0.8 -> 28 / 27 / 7 / 12. Old behaviour was vehicle 7, medium+heavy 1.

Coherence fixes found while editing: produce-bridge-infantry is a BAND (count(e1) >= X and < X + extras) sitting on top of produce-infantry's cap, so both bounds had to move together or the band would break; and infantry-reserves asks 'is the vehicle complement full' against the same cap expression, so that reference was updated too.

Acceptance corpus: it is frozen and CANNOT be regenerated (CompileDoctrine is deleted), so a param added afterwards has no value in it and every test failed to bind. Added POST_FREEZE_PARAMS in tests/acceptance.rs binding force-size to 0 — the off position, which is exactly the world the frozen rows describe — with the reasoning recorded there. One new RETUNED entry (produce-infantry-rush); the other ten army-cap rules already had Field::Condition entries. The produce-vehicle entry carries the full rationale.

Tests: vimyc 170 passed / 0 failed (cargo exit 0). vimy-core and currie go test exit 0. Added TestDoctrineParamsCarriesForceSize covering both the 0.8 case and that a zero doctrine still EMITS the key — a silently absent param compiles to a cap of zero rather than failing, which would be a nasty way to lose an army.

NOT yet validated in a game. force_size only takes effect if the strategist actually sets it; if it leaves it at 0 the caps still improve via (a) and (b) but the ceiling stays at the default.

title: Scouts are driven into the enemy base all game, and the scout is preferentially a light tank
description:
Observed by the user watching game 102: 'vimy was also sending solo tanks, that would get quickly destroyed with tesla and flame towers'.

Mechanism, confirmed in code:
1. ActionScoutPatrol (actions.go:1172) computes targetKnownBase := scoutReach > 0.5 && NearestEnemyBase() != nil, and when true sets wp = {base.X, base.Y} — the scout is ordered INTO the enemy base, not around a perimeter.
2. scout_reach_priority was >0.5 in 30/30 doctrine windows of game 102 (median 0.75), so this held for the whole game.
3. scout-with-scouts (micro.vy) has NO 'require not has-enemy-intel()' guard — unlike scout-with-idle-units, which got one earlier. Its because string is 'rangers keep patrolling so intel stays fresh', so it re-issues the order every time the scout goes idle, for the rest of the game.
4. designateScout (env.go:946) picks the scout 'preferring a light tank for survivability and vision', then an attack dog. A 700-credit combat vehicle becomes a solo suicide scout.

The code comment states the intent — 'once we know where it is, the perimeter rotation is spent on corners that no longer matter' — so targeting the base is meant to END the search, but it never terminates and aims at the base centre.

Game 102 context: no ranger and no attack dog were ever built (produce-scout-vehicle acted 0; it acted 1 in games 96,97,98,99,101). Peak light tank was 1, first at 17700, and scout-with-scouts last acted at 17960. Cannot prove from the export which unit was driven early (scout-with-scouts acted from 2400 with no ranger/dog/light-tank present), so the early-game driver is unconfirmed — but the mechanism and the late-game light tank are both solid.

Possible interaction with vimy-2kx: produce-scout-vehicle uses reserves(500), which the new depot clause raises to ~1500 during the pre-depot window — exactly the window where 'require not has-enemy-intel()' lets it fire. Games 100 and 102 are the only two that built no scout vehicle, and 102 is the first with the clause. Worth checking before blaming the clause, since 100 predates it.

Fix options:
(a) Gate the base-targeting on the search still being open: targetKnownBase should also require !HasEnemyIntel(), so the scout drives at the base to FIND it and stops once found.
(b) Add 'require not has-enemy-intel()' to scout-with-scouts, mirroring scout-with-idle-units. Simplest and most consistent, but ends ongoing patrol entirely.
(c) Never designate a combat vehicle as scout while combat vehicles are scarce.

(a) is the most faithful to the stated intent; (c) is worth doing regardless.

comments.author: Nathan Stehr
comments.text:
Implemented (a) and (c).

(a) actions.go ActionScoutPatrol: targetKnownBase now also requires !env.HasEnemyIntel(). HasEnemyIntel needs a BUILDING sighting, so the scout still drives at a base location inferred from patrols in order to confirm it, then stops once the buildings are actually seen and reverts to perimeter rotation. This matches the code comment's stated intent ('once we know where it is...') which previously never terminated.

(c) env.go designateScout: reordered so the attack dog is taken first — it is the disposable one and a scout is spent sooner or later — and the light tank is only designated when CombatVehicleCount() > lightTankScoutMinVehicles (3, new const in actions.go). Game 102 peaked at three combat vehicles and put its only light tank on patrol.

Note for Allied factions: with no dog available and armour under the threshold, no scout is designated at all, so scout-with-scouts will not fire (count(idle-scouts) == 0). That is deliberate — the Allied answer is the ranger via produce-scout-vehicle, and scout-with-idle-units still covers early recon. If ranger production stays broken (see the vimy-2kx interaction note) Allied patrol scouting will simply be absent rather than suicidal.

Tests: replaced TestDesignateScout_PrefersLightTankOverDog, which encoded the old preference, with TestDesignateScout_PrefersDogOverLightTank plus TestDesignateScout_LightTankOnlyWhenArmourCanSpareIt covering both branches (3 vehicles -> no scout; 4 -> light tank designated). vimy-core go test exits 0; vimyc 170 passed / 0 failed (no .vy changed, corpus unaffected).

title: reserves() has no service-depot clause — armour never arrives
description:
Service depot costs exactly 1200; build-service-depot's 'cash >= service-depot-cash()' (1200) is a zero-reserve gate and CANNOT be lowered. But reserves() in core.vy:10 protects savings for radar, war-factory and tech-center with no equivalent clause for the depot, so every cheaper rule spends the cash first and the depot waits for a rare spike.

Evidence (games 98,99,100,101): depot built at ticks 17170, 14800, never, 19820. Medium tank (2TNK, 850) is depot-gated; first medium tank at 24900, 17400, never, 30450, with PEAK medium tanks of 1,2,0,1. Artillery also costs 850 and is NOT depot-gated, which is why Vimy appears to 'prefer artillery' — it is the only 850 vehicle it can build. Directive says 'mass medium tanks'; peak armour across all four games is ~6 vehicles while produce-vehicle acts 21-23 times.

Proposed fix: add a fourth clause to reserves() in the existing idiom, e.g.
  and (vehicle-weight <= 0.3 or has-role(service-depot) or not has-role(war-factory)
       or cash >= cost + min(cost * 2, 1200))
Escapes on low vehicle-weight and on not-yet-having-a-war-factory. Consider an is-rushed() escape too: defences are what keep Vimy alive (game 100 died with 1 defence, game 101 survived 36780 ticks with 9), so this must not starve build-base-defense during a rush.

Needs a RETUNED entry (Field::Condition) against the frozen acceptance corpus.

comments.author: Nathan Stehr
comments.text:
Implemented. Added one clause to reserves() (core.vy) and scaled-reserves() (production.vy):

  and (vehicle-weight <= 0.3 or has-role(service-depot) or not has-role(war-factory)
       or not can-build-role(service-depot)
       or cash >= cost + min(cost * 2, 1200))

Corrections to the original analysis while implementing:
- The priority theory was wrong. The depot at 679 does outrank build-second-refinery (673 at economy_priority 0.8) and sits below build-advanced-power (790), which took 4 slots in game 101. But raising priority would not have helped: in 257 sampled game-101 states WITH a war factory and before the depot was bought, cash >= 1200 held in exactly 1. The depot was never affordable, not outranked.
- 16 of the 17 pre-depot states where cash reached 1200 were BEFORE the war factory existed. The factory arrives and vehicle production drains the cash from then on, which is exactly the window this clause brakes.
- affordable() (buildings.vy:35) ALREADY had a service-depot clause, gated on income-rate > 0. So the idea existed for buildings; this extends it to unit production. build-base-defense is untouched — it uses affordable(), not reserves(), so there is no defence-starvation risk and the is-rushed escape I first proposed was unnecessary.

Effect at the min(cost*2,1200) shape: rifle 100 -> needs 300 (reachable in 60% of game-101 pre-depot states, so infantry keeps flowing); light tank 700 -> 1900 and artillery 850 -> 2050 (4%), so the 700-850 vehicles that compete with the depot's 1200 hold back. Defences unaffected.

No army vacuum during the save-up window. Bonus: produce-spy fell to 1 (from 6 in game 101) since infantry-reserves now brakes it too — partial relief for vimy-cui without touching that rule.

title: Building rules double-produce: only build-radar guards against producing a second before the first is placed
description:
Observed live in game 89: three barracks, with infantry_weight never above 0.25 all game — so build-extra-barracks (which requires > 0.6) was never in the compiled rule set. The extras came from build-barracks firing repeatedly.

Construction is two steps: produce (StartProduction), then place (PlaceBuilding). A produced-but-unplaced building has no role, so:

  1. produce a barracks; queue-busy(Building) clears when production finishes
  2. it is not placed yet, so not has-role(barracks) still holds
  3. the rule fires again and produces another
  4. repeat until one lands

build-barracks guards only on:
  require not queue-busy(Building)
  require not has-role(barracks)

build-radar is the ONLY rule in buildings.vy carrying the actual guard:
  require not queue-producing-role(radar)

So this was diagnosed once, fixed for radar, and never generalised. Every other building rule — barracks, war factory, airfield, service depot, tech centre, refineries, defences — has the same hole.

Why it surfaced now: the gate is cash >= 300. With cash pinned near zero in games 85-87 the AI could not afford to double-produce. Raising the harvester cap on 2026-09-08 (refinery+1 -> refinery*2) funded it, so an economy fix exposed a latent construction bug. Expect the same on more expensive buildings as income rises further.

Fix: add require not queue-producing-role(<role>) to every build-* rule that currently guards only on not has-role(). Cheap and mechanical. Worth also checking whether place-ready-building places every ready building or one per tick, since that sets how many can pile up.
notes:
CONFIRMED IN PLAY, and via a different rule than the barracks case.

Game 99 built three helipads. Not build-airfield firing repeatedly — build-extra-airfield acted 3 times, at an air_weight of 0.06 to 0.15 all game.

Its cap is:
  require aircraft-capacity < lerp(2, 8, air-weight)

At air_weight 0.12 that permits 2 pads. aircraft-capacity counts PLACED buildings, and construction is produce-then-place, so three could be produced before any of them landed and the cap read as satisfied throughout.

Cost: roughly 1500 credits in a game where build-base-defense could not afford 540 in 90% of states and managed 9 structures. That is three defences.

Both airfield rules now carry require not queue-producing-role(airfield). Still unguarded: build-barracks, build-war-factory, build-service-depot, build-tech-center, the refineries, and the defence rules. build-radar has carried the guard since before this session, which is how the shape was recognised.

Worth noting the general form: ANY cap expressed over a role count is defeated by this, not just the not-has-role guards. That is why build-extra-airfield failed despite having a numeric cap.
close_reason:
Seventeen build rules now carry require not queue-producing-role(<what they build>).

The general form, which was worse than the issue originally said: construction is produce-then-place, so ANY limit expressed over a role count is satisfied the whole time an unplaced building sits waiting. That covers not-has-role guards and numeric caps alike — game 99 built three helipads under a cap of two, because aircraft-capacity counts placed pads.

Guarded: barracks (x3 rules), war factory (x2), service depot, tech centre, refineries (x3), naval yards (x2), airfields (x2), aa-defense, gap generator, iron curtain, missile silo, ore silo.

Deliberately NOT guarded, and each for a reason:
  - build-base-defense and build-base-defense-rush choose among several defence types at runtime, so there is no single role literal to name. Over-building defences is also the one overbuild aligned with what we want: they were unaffordable in 90% of game 97's states.
  - build-power and build-advanced-power gate on power-excess < 0, a dynamic condition rather than a role cap. Double-building power during a shortage is arguably right.

Fifteen RETUNED entries record the divergence from Go, all sharing one explanation.

title: ground-defense squad must form at full size while ground-attack forms at 60%, so raising ground_defense_priority makes defending harder
description:
Game 83, three ground squads competing for one unassigned-idle-ground pool:

  harvester-guard  target lerp(2,4,econ 0.70)=3   bar 3   (100%)
  ground-attack    target group-size 6            bar 3   ( 60%)  <- ground-form-threshold()
  ground-defense   target lerp(2,5,gd 0.65)=4     bar 4   (100%)

The pool reached 3 and harvester-guard took it; rebuilt to 3 and ground-attack took it. ground-defense needs 4, never got there, and did not form. It loses on threshold, not priority — its higher priority cannot help if it never clears its own bar while cheaper rules drain the pool.

Worse, the scaling is inverted: lerp(2,5,gd) means a HIGHER ground_defense_priority RAISES the bar (0.3 -> 2, 0.7 -> 4). The strategist's retrieved memory repeatedly advises raising ground_def; each compliance makes the defence squad less able to exist. Game 82 ran gd=0.75 and formed no defence squad; game 83 ran 0.65-0.70 and did the same.

Fix: keep target at lerp(2,5,gd) but let it form at ~60% and fill by reinforcement, matching ground-attack. Same clause as the surplus removal made 2026-09-08.

Note this is downstream of the already-fixed surplus: removing '+ ground-form-threshold()' took it from 0% to 10.7% of game 82 states, but the remaining full-size bar still loses the race in practice.
notes:
CORRECTION + stronger evidence (game 83, 13:48:51):

The squad DID eventually form — the original text said it did not. It formed at size 3 / target 3, in the window where ground_defense_priority hit 0.45.

ground_defense_priority values chosen across game 83: 0.70, 0.65, 0.60, 0.50, 0.45.
Bar = lerp(2,5,gd): 4 at 0.60-0.70, 3 at 0.45-0.50.
Competitors' bar: 3 (harvester-guard and ground-attack both).

The defence squad formed in exactly one window: gd=0.45, the LOWEST value of the game — the only point where its bar matched its competitors' and it could win the pool race.

This is the inversion demonstrated end to end: the doctrine had to care less about defence in order to obtain a defence squad. Fix as described.

title: reserves() superweapon escape clause is Soviet-only, taxing Allied factions permanently
description:
core.vy reserves() has:

  and (superweapon-priority <= 0.4 or has-role(missile-silo) or has-role(iron-curtain)
       or not has-role(tech-center) or cash >= cost + min(cost * 3, 2500))

Every escape is Soviet. An Allied faction that builds a tech centre while superweapon_priority > 0.4 can never satisfy it, so it pays a permanent +2500 reserve on every purchase for the rest of the game — the same reserve tax diagnosed and capped on 2026-09-07, reappearing through a faction door.

Not triggered in game 83 only because the strategist happened to pick superweapon_priority 0.20.

Also: factionLockedRoles covers units only, no buildings. So can-build-role lies about superweapon structures, and fire-nuke / fire-iron-curtain sit inert in every Allied rule set. Add the superweapon buildings to the table and name the Allied superweapon in the clause.

title: Faction filter deletes preferences but never re-plans
description:
Game 83 (germany/Allied, directive 'air superiority ... rockets from the ground to take out any anti-air'): preferred_vehicle was [v2_launcher, flak_truck, medium_tank]. The faction filter correctly dropped both Soviet entries, promoting medium_tank.

But the doctrine kept every weight that assumed the dropped units: ground_target_aa_priority 0.90, vehicle_weight 0.35, infantry_weight 0.10. So the plan became 'hunt enemy AA hard, using medium tanks' — short-ranged units sent at anti-air — while the only surviving carrier of the SEAD intent (rocket_soldier) sits in the lowest-weighted category.

Germany has a long-range ground answer: artillery. Nothing substituted it.

Fix direction: stop asking the LLM for unit names. Have it name capabilities (long-range-siege, mobile-aa) and let Go resolve per faction, so the plan survives the faction it is played on.
notes:
The mechanism this issue asks for ALREADY EXISTS in the codebase, for buildings.

roles.go:219
  "airfield": {queue: QueueBuilding, types: []string{Airfield, Helipad}}

The role is a capability. build-airfield fires and the engine resolves it to afld for Soviets and hpad for Allies. The rule never names a type. Confirmed live in game 84: england built 15 helipads via build-airfield, while my own grep for 'afld' found zero and I briefly mis-called it a starved rule.

That is why buildings have had NO faction bug in any game today, while units have had one in every Allied game: preferred_infantry / preferred_vehicle / preferred_aircraft are raw type strings written by the LLM, so no role table ever gets to translate them. DoctrineParams then reads those names and moves rule priorities on the strength of them.

So the fix is not new machinery, it is extending existing machinery one field over:
  - have the strategist name ROLES (long-range-siege, mobile-aa, heavy-armour), not types
  - resolve them through the same table build-airfield already uses
  - FilterPreferences then has nothing left to drop, because an unbuildable role cannot be named

Evidence it matters: game 84 (england, same directive as 83) chose preferred_vehicle [artillery, medium_tank, light_tank] and built arty x30 / 1tnk x20. Game 83 (germany, same directive) demanded v2_launcher in eight consecutive windows, had it dropped every time, and its first ground vehicle arrived at 72% of the game. The faction_side prompt fix got us there this time, but it relies on the model complying; the role table would make it structural.

title: deploy-mcv retries the same failed tile forever; bot could not rebuild for the last fifth of a game
description:
Observed in game 74 (44,370 ticks, lost). The construction yard was destroyed
around tick 34,900, recover-mcv built a replacement MCV, and deploy-mcv then
fired 845 times from tick 35,930 to the end of the game without ever succeeding.
place-ready-building last fired at 18,320. So the bot spent the final 8,440
ticks — a fifth of the game — unable to build anything at all.

    deploy-mcv           845 firings   35,930 - 44,370
    recover-mcv            2 firings   34,920, 35,920
    place-ready-building  23 firings   1,400 - 18,320
    "relocating stuck MCV"  31 log lines

The retry loop exists and ran; it just cannot succeed.

Mechanism
---------
ActionDeployMCV tries Deploy up to mcvMaxDeployAttempts (3), then moves the MCV
to mcvFallbackLocation and resets the counter. Forever, on a 50-tick cooldown.

mcvFallbackLocation is deterministic. It takes the building centroid, walks a
fixed list of 8 offsets, and returns the first that is Land:

    offsets := [8][2]int{{300,0},{-300,0},{0,300},{0,-300}, ...}
    for _, o := range offsets { if Land { return } }

Same inputs, same answer. So all 31 relocations sent the MCV to the SAME TILE,
and each was followed by three more deploys at the spot that had already failed
three times. The loop has no memory of where it has already tried.

Two compounding problems:

1. No diversity. A failed location is retried indefinitely because nothing
   records that it failed.
2. The centroid is the wrong anchor when the base is being overrun. It is derived
   from remaining buildings, so as the base is destroyed the fallback converges on
   wherever the fighting is — which is the least likely place a deploy succeeds.

And nothing reports the failure. The strategist re-planned repeatedly through
those 8,440 ticks with no signal that its commander could not build, so it kept
issuing doctrines whose build orders were unreachable.

Fix
---
- Record attempted locations per MCV and exclude them from the next choice, so
  relocation actually explores.
- Prefer somewhere away from the fighting over the building centroid: the
  centroid is right when expanding, wrong when losing.
- Give up loudly. After N distinct locations have failed, emit an event the
  strategist can see. "I cannot rebuild" is exactly the sort of thing a doctrine
  should respond to, and today it is invisible.

Whether the deploy is being refused for a reason vimy can observe (blocked
footprint, enemy proximity) is worth finding out from the mod side first — the
fix above assumes it cannot, which is the safe assumption but maybe not the true
one.

Port note: no rule change. deploy-mcv's condition is right; the action beneath it
cannot make progress.
close_reason:
mcvFallbackLocation now takes the MCV and a per-MCV relocation counter. Anchored on the unit rather than the building centroid (which converged on the fighting as the base shrank), with the counter rotating the starting direction and widening the ring each round, capped at 3 rings so it cannot walk off the map.

Two tests: six relocations must yield at least four distinct tiles (the old pure-centroid version yielded one), and the fallback must stay near the MCV rather than drift toward a surviving building.

Evidence it was still live: game 85, deploy-mcv matched 336 / acted 39 from tick 24820, over the last quarter of a game spent unable to rebuild after losing the construction yard at 20860.

title: No rule defends harvesters in the field; 35% of learned lessons ask for escorts that cannot exist
description:
The rule set has no way to defend the economy in the field, and the LLM has
learned at high confidence that it should.

Evidence
--------
82 of 234 archived lessons (35%) tell the strategist to assign escorts or keep a
mobile guard. 114 mention harvesters, at mean confidence 0.82. Samples:

  "...assign escorts or dispersed harvesters - do not persist in pure V2/barrage
   + tank doctrines while harvesters are being farmed"
  "...or add dedicated escort units - sustained tank-focused stances will not
   substitute for base protection"

There is no such action. The whole defensive vocabulary is:

  defend-base  air-defend-base  naval-defend-base
  emergency-defend-base  defend-critical-building

Every one is anchored at the base. defend-base and its variants gate on
BaseUnderAttack(); defend-critical-building on CriticalBuildingUnderAttack(). A
harvester being shot at an ore patch triggers none of them.

The only rule that responds to a threatened harvester is flee-harvesters, which
runs it home. That protects the harvester and abandons the ore.

Consequence
-----------
The knobs the LLM can actually set do not do what it has concluded it needs.
Raising ground_defense_priority builds pillboxes and tesla coils AT THE BASE.
Raising economy_priority builds more refineries and harvesters into the same
raids. Neither puts a unit next to a harvester.

Observed in games 71, 73 and 74: sustained harvester_under_attack and
harvester_lost events, economy_crisis, and post-game reviews that say the loss
came from raids rather than from production. Game 73 built 19 combat vehicles and
still lost the economy — the army existed and was in the wrong place.

This is the interesting failure now that the tech and cash bugs are fixed. It is
also a a case of the strategist learning something true and unusable: 35% of its
lessons ask for behaviour the rule set cannot express, which quietly degrades the
value of the lesson archive.

Shape of a fix
--------------
Needs an action and a rule, not a knob:

  - an action that assigns idle combat units to guard harvesters or the ore
    patches being worked, distinct from squad formation so it does not compete
    with the attack squad
  - a rule gated on harvesters being under attack rather than on the base being
    under attack - HarvestersInDanger already exists and now weighs threat
    (vimy-mfq), so the condition is available
  - probably a doctrine parameter so the LLM can ask for it, since it already
    tries to

Worth deciding whether escorting is a squad role (the squad machinery already
has domains and roles) or a lighter assignment. A squad role would reuse
form-squad, SquadDefend and the existing memory, which argues for it.
notes:
PARTLY RESOLVED EARLIER, remaining half fixed 2026-09-08.

The rule this issue asks for now exists: guard-harvesters sends the harvester-guard squad to attack-move on whichever threatened harvester is nearest the squad. That closed the 'no vocabulary' half.

But it barely fired. Games 84+85 combined:
  return-idle-harvesters  matched 1112  acted 100
  flee-harvesters         matched 1058  acted 241
  form-harvester-guard    matched    8  acted   8
  guard-harvesters        matched    5  acted   5

economy_priority ran 0.7-0.85, far above the rule's 0.3 gate, and the squad existed. The blocker was idleness, asserted in TWO places: the rule required squad-idle-count(harvester-guard) > 0, and the action itself used squadIdleActorIDs. A guard squad already riding to one raid is not idle, and harassment is continuous, so after the first response the squad could never be re-tasked.

Fix: squadCommittableActorIDs (every member not retreating, idle or not), the idle requirement dropped from the rule, and a 100-tick resend throttle keyed on the target so re-ordering does not cancel the in-flight path — the failure ActionScoutWithIdleUnits carries a comment about (772 attack_move commands in one game).

Still open in principle: the doctrine has no way to ASSIGN escorts to a specific harvester, only to answer a raid after it starts.

title: Harvesters oscillate when any single enemy is near: flee and return fight each other
description:
Observed live 2026-09-04 during a game on vimyc-compiled rules. After an attack was
repelled, harvesters shuttled to the refinery and back without ever harvesting. It
resolved on its own when a single enemy rifleman near the base was killed.

Mechanism
---------
Two rules issue contradictory orders to the same units, and nothing stops them:

    flee-harvesters        priority lerp(150,300,economy)  category micro
    return-idle-harvesters priority 100                    category harvester

Different categories, both non-exclusive, so exclusivity cannot arbitrate. The
cycle is: flee moves the harvester away -> it goes idle -> return-idle-harvesters
sends it a Harvest order at the refinery's coordinates (actions.go:1422, the target
is the refinery, not an ore field) -> the threat is still in range -> flee again.
That is exactly 'back and forth to the refinery, never picking up minerals'.

Trigger
-------
HarvestersInDanger (env.go:631) counts ANY enemy within the radius, with no notion
of what it is:

    for _, en := range e.State.Enemies {
        if dx*dx+dy*dy < threshSq { out = append(out, u); break }
    }

One e1 rifleman is indistinguishable from a mammoth tank. dangerPct is
lerpf(0.05,0.15,economy), so an economy-focused doctrine has the LARGEST danger
radius — the doctrines that most need harvesting are the most easily stalled.

Fixes, in order of preference
-----------------------------
1. Make the danger test threat-aware rather than presence-aware: weigh the enemy
   by what it is, or require more than one, or require the harvester to be taking
   damage. A single rifleman should not stop an economy; a tank column should.
2. Stop the two rules contradicting each other. Either put them in one category so
   exclusivity arbitrates, or have ActionSendIdleHarvesters skip harvesters the
   flee action moved this window (Memory already carries a 'harvestSent' map, so
   a 'fled' set is the same shape).

(1) alone leaves the oscillation for a real threat, which is arguably correct —
fleeing from a tank and returning when it leaves is the intended behaviour. (2)
alone leaves one rifleman able to park the economy indefinitely. Both are worth
doing, and (1) is the one that was actually observed.

Port note: (1) is a predicate change in Go and needs no rule edit. (2) as a
category change is a rule edit and would need to land in doctrine.vy too.
notes:
Both halves fixed 2026-09-04, from game 71 (id 71, lost, 27,570 ticks).

Evidence that made the case: flee-harvesters fired 696 times against 486 returns
between ticks 8,900 and 26,190 — two thirds of the game — and the post-game review
recorded an economy_crisis when all harvesters were lost. Cash was 0 from tick
4,500 onward, which starved the vehicle reserves added by vimy-tex: two combat
vehicles in the whole game.

(1) HarvestersInDanger now weighs the threat rather than counting presence. Enemy
HP within range is summed and compared against the harvester's own MaxHP —
relative, matching SquadThreatRatio, so no table of unit health to maintain and
nothing to drift when the mod changes one. HarvesterThreatRatio = 0.5. A lone
rifleman does not qualify, seven do, one tank does.

Full HP rather than current, deliberately: a harvester already down to a sliver
should not become easier to spook as it takes damage.

(2) ActionSendIdleHarvesters skips harvesters in the harvesterFleeing map.
Sharing a category was not an option — micro is non-exclusive by design, so its
rules co-fire and exclusivity cannot arbitrate between them.

The mechanism was worse than the description guessed: FleeHarvesters sends the
harvester to the NEAREST REFINERY, and so does ActionSendIdleHarvesters. Both
orders pointed at the same place, which is exactly why it looked like shuttling
to the refinery rather than fleeing anywhere. The flee map is already pruned to
harvesters still in danger, so the guard clears itself.

Neither is a rule change, so vimyc is untouched. Verified by mutation: making the
threat test always true, and the flee guard never fire, each fail their test.

Left open until a game shows harvesters harvesting through a raid.

title: Post-game review infers outcomes from doctrines, persists wrong lessons at high confidence
description:
The post-game reviewer reasons over the doctrines that were REQUESTED, not over what
the game actually produced, and in game 68 that produced confidently wrong lessons
which are now stored at confidence 0.9 and will be injected into future games.

Game 68 built zero tanks. Ever. Peak heavy-tank 0, medium-tank 0, v2-launcher 0
(state dump export-20260903-215147.json). Twelve vehicles were produced across 32,500
ticks and all twelve were flak trucks, because radar was never built and the Vehicle
queue never offered anything else (see vimy-tex, vimy-77s).

The review the LLM wrote (games.review_json, id=68):

  "The commander repeatedly pursued vehicle-focused tank-wave doctrines (vehicle
   weight ~0.5-0.62) ... the tank-heavy approach failed to stop economic attrition
   that cost the game."

And the lessons it persisted (lessons table, game_id=68):

  conf 0.90  "...suspend large nonessential tank-wave production until harassment is
              suppressed"
  conf 0.85  "Allocate a fraction of forces to local economy defense ... rather than
              only scaling tanks"

There was no tank-wave production to suspend and no tanks being scaled. The reviewer
saw vehicle_weight 0.5-0.62 in the archived doctrines and inferred an army that never
existed. Its diagnosis inverts the actual failure: the problem was not too much
armour, it was that the doctrine's armour was unreachable and the cash leaked into
flak trucks and rifles instead.

Why this matters more than one bad review
-----------------------------------------
These lessons feed back into the strategist (see "memory injected" at session start).
A 0.9-confidence lesson telling future games to cut tank production is actively
harmful given the real bug is that tanks never get built. The failure mode compounds:
the worse the execution gap, the more confidently the reviewer misattributes it.

Fix
---
Give the reviewer ground truth about outcomes, not just intentions. The data already
exists — rule_firings is recorded per doctrine, and the state dump carries per-role
counts. Concretely:
  - Feed the review prompt a production summary (units actually produced per role,
    peak alive per role, buildings ever completed) alongside the archived doctrines.
  - Feed it the doctrine-vs-reality gap explicitly: for each doctrine, its preferred
    units and how many of those were actually produced while it was in force. A
    doctrine that asked for heavy_tank 46 times and produced 0 should be impossible
    for the reviewer to miss.
  - Consider a mechanical guard before persisting a lesson: if a lesson's guidance
    names a unit or role, check that role was actually produced in the game. If it
    was not, the lesson is about something that did not happen — drop it or flag it
    for review rather than storing it at 0.9.

The third lesson from game 68 ("maintain moderate tech investment while moving forces
to guard duty", conf 0.6) is the only one that points at the real problem, and it is
stored at the lowest confidence of the three.

Consider purging or down-weighting the two bad game-68 lessons before the next run so
they do not steer it.

Port note: this is the strategist/review layer, not the rule engine, so it likely
survives the Rust port unchanged and should be fixed independently of it.

title: No cash reservation for radar deadlocks vehicle tech (no tanks all game)
description:
Observed live (game of 2026-09-03, /tmp/vimy.log, ~21k ticks, Soviet, combined-arms
doctrine asking for [heavy_tank medium_tank flak_truck v2_launcher]): zero tanks were
ever produced because the radar dome was never built, and without `dome` the RA
prerequisite `vehicles.upgraded` is missing, so 3tnk / v2rl never enter the Vehicle
queue at all.

Evidence
--------
Building queue offered `dome` for the entire game (238 consecutive diagnostic samples)
and it was never queued:

    queue=Building busy=false currentItem="" buildable=spen,dome,weap,proc,powr,barr,kenn,fix

Vehicle queue, all game:

    queue=Vehicle busy=false currentItem="" buildable=harv,apc,truk,ftrk

Cash flow:

    tick=2000   total_available=1200
    tick=2500   total_available=0
    tick=9500   total_available=820    <- peak for the remaining 12k ticks
    tick=19500  total_available=653

Root cause
----------
`build-radar` (rules/compiler_buildings.go:45) hard-gates on `Cash() >= 1000`
(Cash() = cash + resources, rules/env.go:110). Nothing reserves cash for the radar:
`initSavings` (rules/compiler.go:154-170) reserves for war_factory (2000) and
tech_center (1500), and both of those reservations are explicitly disarmed while
`!HasRole("radar")` — so in the window where radar is the thing we need, the savings
list is empty. Income arrives in 250-500 dribbles and the cheap rules (produce-infantry
at 100-300, base defense, produce-flak-truck at 600) drain it before it can ever reach
1000. Permanent deadlock: no radar -> no tanks -> the doctrine's stated plan is
unreachable for the rest of the game.

This is the upstream cause of the flak-truck spam in vimy-77s: flak_truck is not
merely winning the priority contest, it is the ONLY buildable combat vehicle.

Fix
---
Add a radar reservation to `c.savings` / `c.infantrySavings` when
`VehicleWeight > DoctrineEnabled` (radar is the vehicle tech gate, not just a
radar-for-its-own-sake building):

    buildingSaving{`HasRole("radar")`, 1000}

Note the existing war_factory / tech_center reservations are conditioned on
`|| !HasRole("radar")` precisely to avoid stacking reserves behind an unbuilt radar —
so the radar reserve itself must be the one that is active in that window, and the
others correctly stay disarmed. Consider also whether the ordering should be
generalized: reserve for the cheapest unmet prerequisite on the path to the doctrine's
preferred unit, rather than a hand-maintained list.

Port note: carry this into the Rust rule engine — it is a savings-model gap, not a
Go-specific bug.
notes:
Fix applied 2026-09-04 in both compilers, with the differential confirming they agree.

Go: initSavings gains `buildingSaving{HasRole("radar"), 1000}` gated on VehicleWeight > DoctrineEnabled, placed first so it is the reserve that is armed in the window where the others are deliberately disarmed.

vimyc: the same clause in the `reserves` and `scaled-reserves` defs of doctrine.vy, scaled by the same select() the other reserves use so produce-vehicle and produce-siege-vehicle stay consistent.

Effect on the doctrine from the reported game (vehicle 0.6, tech 0.6):
  produce-infantry     Cash() >= 100 && (HasRole("radar") || Cash() >= 1100)
  produce-flak-truck   Cash() >= 600 && (HasRole("radar") || Cash() >= 1600)
Cheap rules can no longer drain income below the 1000 build-radar needs.

The acceptance test still matches on 45,635 rules across 532 doctrines, so the
two implementations agree with the fix in place.

Left open: this is verified as a rule change, not as behaviour. It needs a game
showing a radar and then tanks.
close_reason:
Verified in game 73 (26,640 ticks, vimyc-compiled rules).

build-radar fired at tick 4,980, against 7,260 in game 71 and never at all in the
game that reported this. The deadlock is gone: the reserve holds cheap production
back, cash reaches 1000, the dome goes up and the vehicle queue opens.

Downstream, 19 combat vehicles were produced against 2 in game 71 — the reserves
this bug was about can only be satisfied once the tech gate opens.

Closed on that evidence. The game was still lost, but on defence and harassment
rather than on an economy that could not tech.

title: Weight-scale vehicle-reserve in infantry savings
description: Game 64 (mech-CA): produce-infantry cash gate was Cash >= 900 (100 base + 800 vehicle reserve) while produce-vehicle needed only Cash >= 800. Vehicle rule fired whenever cash hit 800, draining it before infantry ever saw the 900 threshold. Result: infantry starved (e1Count stuck at 8, decaying to 6) while 20 tanks got queued. Fix: scale the 800 vehicle reservation by max(0, vehicle_weight - infantry_weight). Combined-arms (inf=0.28, veh=0.62) gets 272 reserve instead of 800. Infantry-heavy (inf > veh) gets zero. Pure-vehicle keeps most of it. Three tests cover the scaling behavior. Diagnostic-driven fix — cash-flow + produce-infantry-gate diagnostics from vimy-o32/8vi pinpointed the issue.
close_reason: Shipped. compiler.go initSavings now scales the 800-cost vehicle reservation by max(0, vehicle_weight - infantry_weight). Combined-arms doctrines (inf=0.28, veh=0.62) get 272 reserve. Infantry-heavy (inf > veh) get zero reserve. Pure-vehicle (inf=0.15, veh=0.8) get most of it. 3 new unit tests cover each regime.

title: Barracks priority floor (745) to beat radar-boosted priority
description: Game 63 (mech-CA): hasBarracks=false through tick 5000 despite doctrine having infantry=0.3 and groundDefense=0.7 (which should make barracks priority 670). Root cause: preferred_vehicle=[medium_tank, ...] triggered prefersRadarGatedPrimary → radar priority bumped to 710, beating barracks (670). Sequence became: power(800) → refinery(750) → power → war_factory(680) → **radar(710)** → advanced_power(790, conditional) → barracks(670, last). Barracks is 300 and unblocks the entire infantry queue — it must always come before radar. Fix: barracks priority floor of 745. Still below power (800) and refinery (750) but above radar (710) and normal WF (680-730). TA-boosted WF (770+) can still outrank when the doctrine is truly APC-first. Test added.
close_reason: Shipped. Barracks priority floor of 745 in compiler_buildings.go. Test TestCompileDoctrine_BarracksBeatsRadarForRadarGatedPref reproduces the game 63 scenario (infantry=0.3, groundDef=0.7, preferred_vehicle=[medium_tank, heavy_tank]) and verifies barracks > radar.

title: Repair cash floor + concurrency cap to prevent economy pin-to-zero
description: Game 62 (mech CA loss): cash-flow diagnostic showed cash pinned at 0 from tick 5000+ through end of game. Ore filled silos (-1000 spikes) but converted-cash disappeared instantly to in-flight repairs. OpenRA drains cash per-tick per active repair; with N damaged buildings all being repaired simultaneously, drain rate exceeded harvester income. Fix: two guards in ActionRepairDamagedBuildings: (1) hard cash floor of $500 — no repair actions at all when below (2) max 2 simultaneous active repairs — cap drain rate so income can support production. Existing repair_budget_ratio + pressure filter + idempotency check retained. Cash should now accumulate for rifles instead of being consumed the instant it converts from ore.
close_reason: Shipped. Two new guards in ActionRepairDamagedBuildings: repairCashFloor=500 (skip entire action when cash below floor) and repairMaxConcurrent=2 (cap simultaneous repairs). Preserves existing budget ratio, pressure filter, and idempotency. All tests pass.

title: Rally-then-attack for squad-attack and squad-attack-known-base
description: User observation: OpenRA AI clusters units before an attack; Vimy squads move as a loose gaggle (fast units sprint ahead, slow units trail) so attacks land piecemeal and enemy focus-fires the lead. Fix: rally-then-attack MVP. New SquadClumped(name, radius) helper checks whether 80% of squad members are within radius of centroid. SquadAttackMove and SquadAttackKnownBase check clumped state on initial commit; if dispersed, issue AttackMove to squad centroid (regroup) instead of the actual target. Persistent squadAttackState in memory prevents oscillation: once committed to attacking a target, no re-regroup for 2000 ticks. Tests cover clumped/dispersed/singleton/missing-squad cases.
close_reason: Shipped. New SquadClumped(name, radius) helper with 80% threshold. SquadAttackMove and SquadAttackKnownBase check clumped state on initial commit; if dispersed, issue rally at centroid. squadAttackState tracks commit per squad; TTL 2000 ticks prevents mid-attack oscillation. 4 tests cover clumped/dispersed/singleton/missing squad cases.

title: Add defend-critical-building rule to engage idle squad units when CY/WF/refinery under attack
description: Game 59 (turtle-with-breakout, 32k tick loss): 2 rocket launchers destroyed the CY while an idle mammoth tank sat in the ground-attack squad. Root cause: vimy-d9q intentionally excludes ground-attack squad members from scramble-base-defense (poach-prevention). emergency-base-defense requires zero idle units, which is not true when squad members are idle at base. So neither rule engages an idle squad member even when a critical building is being destroyed. Fix: new defend-critical-building rule at priority 360 (above scramble/emergency), condition CriticalBuildingUnderAttack, action pulls ALL near-base ground units regardless of squad membership. Tests cover detection edge cases.
close_reason: Shipped. New rule defend-critical-building at priority 360 (above scramble 350 and emergency 349).
