Fires on CriticalBuildingUnderAttack (enemy within 10 cells of any CY/WF/refinery/power/barracks). Pulls NearBaseGroundUnits regardless of squad membership. Tests: detection near CY, ignores distant, ignores non-critical buildings, ignores harvester enemies.

title: Add tempo knobs (commit_ratio, base_defense_floor, repair_budget_ratio, scout_reach_priority) and situation signals
description: Add four LLM-tunable doctrine knobs and three situation-context signals per the design discussion. All zero-defaults preserve prior behavior; each knob is cross-cutting (turtle, balanced, and rush doctrines each pick different values on the same axis). Ships behind BAML schema changes with prompt guidance.
close_reason: Shipped. 4 doctrine knobs (commit_ratio, base_defense_floor, repair_budget_ratio, scout_reach_priority) wired end-to-end from BAML through to rules-engine behavior. 3 situation signals (ground_squad_ready_ratio, cash_burn_rate, time_to_reach_enemy_estimate) computed and passed to LLM. Zero-defaults preserve current behavior. 4 new tests cover commit_ratio and base_defense_floor gates. All tests pass.

title: squad-attack-known-base fires even with visible enemies, prefers base for aggressive doctrines
description: Game 49 (35.9k tick loss) showed squad-attack-known-base fire only 2 times despite intel persisting all game (thanks to vimy-sl4). Root cause: rule required !EnemiesVisible AND HasEnemyIntel. Persistent raiders near base kept enemies visible, so the fallback rule never fired even though vimy knew where the enemy base was. squad-attack fired instead (visible enemy path) and pointed the squad at local raiders — never the strategic target. Fix: 1. Removed !EnemiesVisible from squad-attack-known-base condition. 2. Moved both squad-attack and squad-attack-known-base to new exclusive category ground_attack_choice so they cannot thrash between destinations in the same tick. 3. When Aggression >= DoctrineSignificant, squad-attack-known-base priority set to c.attackPriority+5 (outranks squad-attack) so aggressive doctrines press the enemy base over swatting raiders. Non-aggressive doctrines keep the historical priority. 4. squad-reengage stayed in combat category non-exclusive so it fires alongside whichever choice won. All tests pass.
close_reason: Shipped. squad-attack and squad-attack-known-base now share exclusive category ground_attack_choice so only one fires per tick. Aggressive doctrines (Aggression >= 0.3) get squad-attack-known-base priority c.attackPriority+5, outranking squad-attack — ground squad presses the base while base defenses handle raiders. Non-aggressive doctrines keep the historical known-base-below-visible priority. squad-reengage stayed in combat/non-exclusive so stragglers still catch up.

title: Enemy base intel wipes from a single scout pass-through — squad-attack-known-base cant fire
description: Live observation: rush doctrine had 17 rifles + 3 dogs but ground-attack squad never deployed. Log analysis showed enemy_base_discovered event at tick 6520, then clearing stale enemy base intel just 30 seconds later. HasEnemyIntel flipped false and stayed false. squad-attack-known-base condition became unsatisfiable. Squad kept forming size=6 but had no target. Fix in updateIntel: intelMinAge 300 -> 3000 ticks; new intelClearSustain=500 tick requirement for continuous our-unit-near + no-enemy before clearing. Prevents scout patrols from wiping intel every rotation. Tests: TestUpdateIntel_ClearsStaleIntel (verifies clearing still works after full sustain window) and TestUpdateIntel_ScoutPassThroughDoesNotClear (verifies scout drive-by doesnt wipe intel).
close_reason: Shipped. intelMinAge 300 -> 3000. New intelClearSustain=500 tick sustained-confirmation gate before clearing. Sustain counter reset when our unit leaves or enemy appears. Two new tests cover both the sustained-clear path and the scout-pass-through must-not-clear path. All tests pass.

title: Drop war-factory cash reservation from rush-mode rules
description:
Game 47 (12.98k tick loss, rush doctrine) fired rush variants 0 times. The vimy-qp1 fix added WF cash reservation (Cash >= 2050) to produce-infantry-rush to prevent game 43 pattern (39 rifles, 0 vehicles). But game 47 showed the reservation was overcorrection: with 483 repair firings + harvester attrition, cash rarely held >= 2050 during rush, so rush rifles never fired and only 20 normal rifles were produced.

Correct human response to a rush is survive first (rifles + pillboxes), tech second. Once IsRushed clears (tick > 10500 or no recent harvester events), normal build rules resume and WF builds via its own path — which respects the c.savings WF reserve gated on radar existing. Since radar is now deferred during rush (vimy-dsb), no WF reserve is active during rush anyway.

Fix: removed WF and airfield reservation clauses from produce-infantry-rush and build-base-defense-rush. Rush rifles now fire at bare Cash >= 50, pillbox-rush at bare Cash >= 200. All tests pass.
close_reason: Shipped. Removed WF/airfield cash reservations from produce-infantry-rush and build-base-defense-rush. Rush rifles fire at Cash >= 50, pillboxes at Cash >= 200. WF gets built via normal build-war-factory path after IsRushed clears.

title: Stop scramble-base-defense from poaching ground-attack squad members
description: Game 46 (21.1k tick rush-doctrine loss): form-ground-attack fired 341 times but squad-attack fired only 1 time. Root cause: scramble-base-defense and ActionDefendBase used IdleGroundUnits which includes ground-attack squad members. Every raider near base poached the squad. Fix: ActionDefendBase uses UnassignedIdleGround; scramble-base-defense condition now checks UnassignedIdleGround. Emergency-base-defense unchanged as last-resort fallback.
close_reason: Shipped. ActionDefendBase uses UnassignedIdleGround. scramble-base-defense condition changed to gate on UnassignedIdleGround. Emergency-base-defense preserved as last-resort fallback (fires only when no idle units at all). All tests pass.

title: Reserve cash for war factory / airfield in rush-mode rules
description:
Game 43 (28.1k tick loss) produced 39 rifles (29 rush + 10 normal) but ZERO combat vehicles — war factory was never built because cash never accumulated to 2000. The rush-mode rules were spending every  of income on rifles as fast as it came in.

Fix: produce-infantry-rush and build-base-defense-rush now reserve cash for production-tier buildings when the doctrine wants them. New rule conditions:

produce-infantry-rush:
  IsRushed() && ... && Cash() >= 50
    && (HasRole(war_factory) || Cash() >= 2050)   // when VehicleWeight > 0.1
    && (HasRole(airfield) || Cash() >= 550)       // when AirWeight > 0.1

build-base-defense-rush:
  IsRushed() && ... && Cash() >= 200
    && (HasRole(war_factory) || Cash() >= 2200)   // when VehicleWeight > 0.1
    && (HasRole(airfield) || Cash() >= 700)       // when AirWeight > 0.1

Reservations apply only when the doctrine wants vehicles/air respectively. Pure infantry/defense doctrines (VehicleWeight=0, AirWeight=0) keep the bare / rush gates.

Acceptance: in the next rush-tempo Germany match where vehicle_weight is doctrinal, build-war-factory should fire within the first few thousand ticks (cash will be reserved instead of immediately spent on rifles). produce-vehicle should fire at least a few times during the game.
close_reason: Implemented. produce-infantry-rush and build-base-defense-rush now reserve cash for war factory (2000) and airfield (500) when doctrine wants vehicles/air respectively. Pure infantry doctrines keep bare / rush gates. All tests pass.

title: Defer non-critical builds during rush window
description:
Game 42 (18.9k tick fast loss): rush variants fired (15 produce-infantry-rush, 3 build-base-defense-rush) but production was still gated. Concurrently, vimy was spending cash on 3x build-extra-refinery + 2x build-advanced-power during the rush window — pure economy expansion while the base was being attacked.

Fix: add !IsRushed() gate to non-survival build rules so they pause until the rush flag clears. Cash flows to rifles/pillboxes instead of expansion. Affected rules:

Economy expansion (compiler_economy.go):
- build-second-refinery
- build-extra-refinery
- build-advanced-power
- build-ore-silo

Tier-up / specialist (compiler_buildings.go):
- build-radar
- build-airfield
- build-service-depot
- build-naval-yard
- build-gap-generator
- build-tech-center
- build-missile-silo / build-iron-curtain
- build-extra-barracks / build-extra-war-factory / build-extra-airfield / build-extra-naval-yard

Kept firing during rush (survival-critical):
- build-power, build-refinery (first), build-barracks, build-war-factory, build-barracks-prereq
- build-base-defense + build-base-defense-rush, build-aa-defense
- build-kennel (cheap, Soviet rush defender enabler — 300 cash for dog production)
- build-flame-tower-for-flamethrower + build-tesla-coil-for-shock-trooper (defenses that double as specialist prereqs)
- All rebuild-* rules (recover destroyed criticals)

Once the rush window closes (tick > 10500 OR no recent harvester pressure), IsRushed() flips false and all deferred rules resume their normal compilation/firing.
close_reason: Implemented. Added !IsRushed() gate to 14 non-survival build rules across compiler_economy.go and compiler_buildings.go. Survival-critical rules (basic power, first refinery, barracks, war factory, all base defenses, AA, kennel, all rebuild-*) unchanged. All tests pass.

title: Repair-spending cap: per-building idempotency + pressure-aware critical-only filter
description:
Game 41 (94.7k tick loss): repair-buildings fired 4900x — more than 3rd place after raid signals. The old action sent a RepairBuilding toggle for EVERY damaged building EVERY eval, with no idempotency. RepairBuilding is a toggle in OpenRA (send once = start, send again = stop), so the constant re-issuance was actively cancelling in-flight repairs and burning cash without completing them. Meanwhile produce-infantry fired only 122x in the same game — the cash imbalance was likely a factor in vimy's 3617 flee-harvesters never being countered.

Two-part fix in ActionRepairDamagedBuildings:

1. Per-building idempotency (repairToggleEntry in memory['repairToggleSent']). Same pattern used by attackOrderEntry/sendAttack. Track the last toggle tick per building ID; re-issue only after repairResendTicks=1500 ticks have elapsed (in case the original was lost). Stops the toggle-storm cancelling in-flight repairs.

2. Pressure-aware filter (isCriticalRepairType): when IsRushed() or IsHarvesterHarassed(), only repair production/economy infrastructure — CY, war factory, barracks, refinery, power plant, advanced power. Skip radar, helipad, tech center, airfield, defenses. The premise is that under sustained raid pressure, vimy can't afford to repair everything; keeping critical production alive matters more than secondary structures.

Test TestIsCriticalRepairType covers the building-type partition.
close_reason: Implemented. ActionRepairDamagedBuildings now tracks per-building toggle state (repairResendTicks=1500) so we don't cancel in-flight repairs. Under pressure (IsRushed or IsHarvesterHarassed), only critical infrastructure types (CY, WF, barracks, refinery, power, advanced power) get repaired — secondary buildings keep damage but cash flows to combat units. Test TestIsCriticalRepairType covers the partition.

title: Drop building-count gate on being_rushed flag
description:
Game 35, 36, 37 all had compiled rush-mode rule variants (produce-infantry-rush, build-base-defense-rush) but the rules never fired. Root cause: the rushMaxBuildingCount condition was being exceeded by tick 9-10k because vimy's normal build order (power + refinery + barracks + war factory + radar + a couple pillboxes + helipad) typically pushes the count past 10-12 buildings before raids arrive.

We tried 6 (original), then 12 — both failed to trigger. The condition isn't pulling its weight because the tick cutoff (rushTickCutoff=10500) already encodes 'early game.' Removed the building-count condition entirely. The rush-mode rules themselves cap their output (produce-infantry-rush cap = 2x infantryCap, build-base-defense-rush uses normal defenseCap) so leaving the flag on throughout the rush window can't produce runaway output — it just lets cheap defenders spawn when the doctrine would otherwise be cash-gated.

Also removed harassMinBuildingCount for symmetry — the tick floor (>=10500) is sufficient for 'mid/late-game.'

Test TestComputePressureFlags_RushClearsAfterTickWindow verifies the flag clears past the tick cutoff (replaces the old building-count test).
close_reason: Removed rushMaxBuildingCount and harassMinBuildingCount gates from computePressureFlags. The tick window alone now determines rush/harass classification (paired with harvester-event detection). Tests updated and passing.

title: Rush-mode rule variants for produce-infantry and build-base-defense
description:
Game 33/34 showed the doctrine layer correctly setting rush-response shape (infantry=0.5, ground_def=0.7, aggression=0.6) but the rules-engine produced almost no rifles (18-19 in 22-30k ticks) and only 9 defenses. The prompt-side rush response can't move cash floors or rule priorities — only the rule layer can.

Implementation:
1. Strategist pushes beingRushed/harvesterHarassed into engine.Memory (mirrors burnedAxes pattern from vimy-bys).
2. New env helpers IsRushed() and IsHarvesterHarassed() expose the flags to rule conditions.
3. New rule produce-infantry-rush: priority infantryBasePri+20, condition gates on IsRushed() && Cash() >= 50 (drops all savings reserves), cap doubled. Coexists with normal produce-infantry; higher priority wins category dispatch when both qualify.
4. New rule build-base-defense-rush: priority defensePriority+100, condition gates on IsRushed() && Cash() >= 200, lifts cash floor above other economy builds so defenses go up before refineries/power. Cap unchanged.

Tests in env_test.go: TestIsRushedAndIsHarvesterHarassed covers helpers. Existing pressure-flag tests pass.

Acceptance: in a rush-tempo game (game-33/34 type), rifle production should significantly outpace prior matches with similar harassment pressure, and base defenses should be built within the first few thousand ticks of rush onset instead of 10k+ ticks later.
close_reason: Implemented. Strategist writes beingRushed/harvesterHarassed to engine.Memory. New env helpers IsRushed() and IsHarvesterHarassed(). Rush-mode variants: produce-infantry-rush (priority+20, Cash>=50, cap 2x) and build-base-defense-rush (priority+100, Cash>=200). Coexist with normal variants; higher priority wins when both qualify. Test TestIsRushedAndIsHarvesterHarassed covers helpers. All other tests pass.

title: MCV deploy never succeeds after CY loss — produces but doesn't redeploy
description:
Game 32 (337k ticks): CY was destroyed around tick 75930 and never rebuilt. recover-mcv fired 8 times (8 MCVs produced) but deploy-mcv fired 25898 times without actually placing a Construction Yard — only 27 place-ready-building firings the entire game. Each MCV sat in the field receiving Deploy commands every 50 ticks until enemy killed it, then recover-mcv produced the next.

Root cause: ActionDeployMCV sends a blind Deploy command for any idle MCV. If the MCV's current position has no valid 3x3 deploy footprint (terrain, nearby buildings, enemy units), the engine silently rejects. The cooldown only throttles the send; nothing tells the MCV to move to a clearer spot.

Fix sketch: track deploy attempt count per MCV (memory[mcvDeployAttempts][id]). After K failed attempts at the current location (e.g. K=3 = ~150 ticks), Move the MCV to a fallback location near our existing infrastructure (e.g. near the war factory or base centroid, offset to find clear land). Reset attempt count on relocation.

Acceptance: with one MCV idle in an undeployable position, after a few deploy retries the MCV is sent a Move order to a fresh location and deploy succeeds at the new spot.
close_reason: Added per-MCV deploy attempt tracking (mcvDeployState in engine memory). After mcvMaxDeployAttempts=3 (~150 ticks of failing Deploy), ActionDeployMCV sends a Move order to a fallback land tile (8 compass offsets around base centroid, picks first Land tile) and resets the attempt counter. When the MCV arrives idle at the new location, Deploy retries fresh. Replaces blind-retry-forever behavior that left 8 MCVs as soft targets across 260k ticks in game 32. All tests pass.

title: Match-long burn buffer + per-axis burn thresholds
description:
Game 31 (85k tick loss) had 71 vehicle-heavy doctrines and only 1 vehicle counter event (Tesla at tick 62060), 23 infantry-heavy doctrines and 1 infantry counter event (Shock Troopers at 31150). burned_axes never triggered for either because (a) the stress-event buffer was pruned at 1500 ticks, so the counter event aged out before being correlated with later pivots, and (b) the threshold required 2 distinct pivot-with-counter pairs.

Two changes shipped:

1. Match-long burn buffer (Strategist.burnStress): mirrors the existing 1500-tick stressEvents but never prunes within a match. computeBurnedAxes walks this. Reset clears on game reset. The original windowed stressEvents stays as-is for LLM-facing situation context.

2. Per-axis burn thresholds (burnedAxisMinPivots map): air = 1 counter (SAM/Flak clusters are permanent), infantry/vehicle/naval = 2 counters (one bad engagement isn't enough to abandon the axis). Air is the highest-cost axis to keep feeding so single-counter burn is justified there.

Tests in agent/strategist_test.go: TestComputeBurnedAxes_AirBurnsAfterOneCounter, TestComputeBurnedAxes_VehicleNeedsTwoCounters, TestComputeBurnedAxes_VehicleBurnsAfterTwoCounters.
close_reason: Implemented as described: Strategist.burnStress (match-long event buffer, never pruned within match) and per-axis burnedAxisMinPivots map {air:1, infantry:2, vehicle:2, naval:2}. Three tests cover the new semantics. All tests pass.

title: Gate produce-aircraft on physical pad capacity to stop cancel-stuck loops
description:
Game 29: cancel-stuck-aircraft fired 120x on 137 produce-aircraft (~87% wasted). Root cause: aircraft cap (lerp 2,8 by air_weight) ignored physical pad capacity (4 per Airfield, 1 per Helipad). When CombatAircraftCount reached pad capacity, completed aircraft sat at 100% with no spawn slot; cancel-stuck-aircraft cancelled them; produce-aircraft re-queued; cycle wasted cash and Aircraft queue time.

Fix: new RuleEnv.AircraftCapacity() returns 4*airfields + 1*helipads. Added !CombatAircraftCount() < AircraftCapacity() guard to produce-aircraft, produce-basic-aircraft, produce-attack-aircraft. When capacity is at limit, production halts; build-extra-airfield (already exists at AirWeight>0.4) takes over and adds another pad.

Edge: at low air_weight (<=0.4) extra-airfield doesn't compile, so 1 airfield = max 4 aircraft regardless of cap. That's a real limit, not a bug. For Allied (helipads only, 1 pad each), extraAirCap=lerp(1,3) may still under-provide vs doctrine cap — flag as follow-up if it shows up in data.

Test TestAircraftCapacity covers the helper.
close_reason: Implemented. New RuleEnv.AircraftCapacity() = 4*airfields + 1*helipads. Added CombatAircraftCount() < AircraftCapacity() guard to produce-aircraft, produce-basic-aircraft, produce-attack-aircraft. Test TestAircraftCapacity covers helper. All tests pass.

title: Recall-overextended yanks squad members from approach waypoints, not just no-mans-land
description:
Game 29 (240k tick loss): recall-overextended-ground-attack fired 554 times, matching the user's live observation that troops kept walking back to base from a parked position in the ore field between bases. Mechanism: BestApproachAxis (vimy-b14) sends squads to a flank waypoint that sits a dozen-plus cells from the enemy base. When the squad arrives at the waypoint and goes idle, OverextendedSquadMembers sees them as far from our base AND outside the 20% enemy-base exemption radius (vimy-91b) — so they get recalled. They walk home, get re-added to ground-attack, attack-move toward waypoint, arrive idle, get recalled. Cycle.

Fix: expand the exemption from 'near enemy base' to 'making forward progress toward enemy base.' Specifically, a unit is overextended only when dist_to_enemy_base >= dist_to_our_base AND beyond the leash. If the unit is closer to any known enemy base than to our base centroid, it's in transit or staging — exempt from recall.

This covers: forward-deployed at base (existing), flank waypoint staging (new), units in transit, units mid-engagement. Doesn't exempt units that genuinely wandered perpendicular to no-man's-land or got pushed past the enemy base.

Acceptance: in TestOverextendedSquadMembers_ExemptsUnitsNearEnemyBase the existing case still passes; add new case where unit at flank staging point (closer to enemy than our base) is also exempted.
close_reason: Replaced fixed-radius enemy-base exemption with forward-progress rule: a unit is overextended only when beyond the leash AND not closer to any known enemy base than to our base centroid. Covers flank-waypoint staging (vimy-b14), units in transit, mid-engagement at enemy base. Updated TestOverextendedSquadMembers_ExemptsUnitsNearEnemyBase to use off-axis position; added TestOverextendedSquadMembers_ExemptsForwardStaging (staging halfway point exempt) and TestOverextendedSquadMembers_FlagsOffAxisWanderer (off-axis wanderer still flagged). All tests pass.

title: Promote burned_axes from prompt-only to hard rule-engine production gate
description:
Game 27 showed aircraft kept being produced (23 over the game) despite 4 separate Flak counter events at ticks 31300, 32770, 54940, 77770. The vimy-b9a burned_axes mechanism set the BAML situation flag correctly but the LLM ignored the soft constraint and kept raising air_weight. Fix: strategist writes the burned set to engine.Memory['burnedAxes'] each evaluation; new RuleEnv.AxisBurned(axis) helper reads it; production rules now hard-gate on !AxisBurned(...):
- produce-aircraft → AxisBurned('air')
- produce-infantry, produce-bridge-infantry, produce-grenadier, produce-rocket-soldier → AxisBurned('infantry')
- produce-vehicle → AxisBurned('vehicle') (siege intentionally NOT gated — siege is the standoff answer to defense clusters)
- produce-ship → AxisBurned('naval')

Specialist/utility rules (attack-dog, specialist-infantry, engineer, spy, siege) intentionally NOT gated so vimy retains some production options when an axis is burned. Test TestAxisBurned in rules/env_test.go covers the helper.
close_reason: Implemented. Strategist writes burnedAxes map to engine.Memory at each eval. New RuleEnv.AxisBurned(axis) helper. Production rules gated: produce-aircraft, produce-infantry, produce-bridge-infantry, produce-grenadier, produce-rocket-soldier, produce-vehicle, produce-ship. Siege/specialist/utility rules intentionally ungated so vimy retains options. Test TestAxisBurned covers the helper.

title: Base defense caps too low to survive sustained raids
description:
Game 24 (England vs Russia, lost in 46.9k ticks): vimy doctrine consistently set ground_defense_priority 0.7-0.85, yet build-base-defense fired only 8 times in 46k ticks and only 15 place-ready-defense (across ground + AA + gap). Critical building lost at tick 18440 (atek). produce-infantry only 17x, produce-vehicle 4x — production died because economy was in shambles from raids the perimeter couldn't stop.

Root cause: rules/compiler_buildings.go:192
  defenseCap := lerp(1, 5, c.d.GroundDefensePriority)
  // gd=0.8 → cap=4, gd=1.0 → cap=5
At gd=0.8 (typical 'hardened' setting) the bot can have AT MOST 4 ground defense structures (pillbox + turret + flame + tesla, summed). For a base with 4+ entry points facing sustained pressure that's far too few — defenders get destroyed faster than the cap allows rebuilds. AA cap is similar: lerp(1, 3, ad) → max 3.

Proposed fix: roughly 2x the caps so a well-defended doctrine can build a real perimeter line.
  defenseCap := lerp(2, 10, c.d.GroundDefensePriority)  // 2..10 instead of 1..5
  aaCap := lerp(2, 5, c.d.AirDefensePriority)            // 2..5 instead of 1..3
A doctrine that sets gd=0.5 still gets a modest 6 ground defenses (was 3). At gd=1.0 you get 10 — enough to cover multiple entry points without going crazy.

The cash gate already throttles spend (lerp 1500..300 cash floor) so this won't cause economy starvation — it just removes the artificial structural ceiling.

Acceptance: in a fresh game, with sustained harvester harassment and high ground_def doctrine, more than 5-6 ground defenses can stand at once. Existing tests still pass.
close_reason: Bumped defense caps. ground defense lerp(1,5,gd) → lerp(2,10,gd); AA lerp(1,3,ad) → lerp(2,5,ad). At gd=0.8 cap is now 8 (was 4), at gd=1.0 it's 10 (was 5). Cash floors unchanged so spend is still throttled. Tests pass.

title: recall-overextended yanks squad members away from enemy base mid-attack
description:
Game 23 (lost vs russia, 126k ticks): user observed 'vimy seemed to have a decisive hold' but the turtle won by attrition. The smoking gun in rule firings: recall-overextended-ground-attack fired 764 times.

Mechanism: at aggression=0.5 (where most of game 23's doctrines sat) the leash is lerpf(0.25, 0.50, 0.5) = 0.375 → ~80 cells on a 150x150 map. OverextendedSquadMembers (rules/env.go:378) flags any IDLE squad member whose distance from OUR building centroid exceeds that radius. RecallOverextended then sends them back to centroid. The intent was 'recall units that wandered into no-man's land after a kill', but in practice when a unit finishes a kill INSIDE the enemy base it goes idle, gets flagged overextended, walks all the way home, gets re-added to the squad, gets attack-ordered back to the enemy base, finishes another kill, idle, recall, repeat. Many of these units die during the walk home or never get to deliver damage.

This perfectly matches the user's observation: vimy holds economically and tactically engages, but never closes the deal.

Fix: a unit is overextended only when it's far from OUR base AND not close to any known enemy base. If the unit is within ~20% diagonal of a remembered enemy base, leave it alone — it's correctly forward-deployed and should rejoin the squad's next attack via squad-reengage rather than being yanked home.

Implementation in rules/env.go OverextendedSquadMembers:
- After computing distance-from-centroid, also compute min distance to any enemy base in env.Memory['enemyBases']
- If that distance is < 0.20 * map_diagonal, skip (don't include in returned slice)

Acceptance: with a remembered enemy base and an idle squad member adjacent to it, OverextendedSquadMembers does not include that unit; with the same member alone in no-man's land far from any enemy base, it is included.
notes: Game 29 follow-up: 20% enemy-base radius was too tight when combined with BestApproachAxis (vimy-b14) flank waypoints. Filed as follow-up to expand to 'making forward progress toward enemy.'
close_reason: OverextendedSquadMembers now exempts units within 20% of map diagonal of any known enemy base. The recall rule fired 764x in game 23, which the user observed as 'vimy held tactically but never closed.' Mechanism: idle squad members near the enemy base were getting yanked all the way home, then re-formed and re-attacked, never delivering decisive damage. Fix in rules/env.go OverextendedSquadMembers: after the leash check, also check distance to enemy bases from memory['enemyBases']; if within enemyBaseExemptPct (0.20) of diagonal, skip. Test: TestOverextendedSquadMembers_ExemptsUnitsNearEnemyBase verifies unit at enemy base position is not flagged while a unit in no-man's-land still is.

title: BURNED AXIS rule misses repeat pivots because recent_doctrines window (8) is too narrow
description:
Game 21 (france vs russia, 91k ticks lost): 4 air pivots across the match (ticks 20060, 41160, 49900, 53880), each followed by aircraft losses to SAM/Flak. BURNED AXIS rule should have prevented the 3rd and 4th — but didn't, because recent_doctrines only shows the last 8 entries and the air pivots were spread 10-20 doctrines apart. Any single evaluation window only sees 0-1 prior air pivots, never 2.

Fix paths (probably both):
1. Widen recent_doctrines window from 8 to 16 — cheap, lets the LLM see longer history.
2. Compute a persistent burned_axes list in strategist.go (similar to stressEvents buffer) — for each axis, mark it burned once 2+ pivots occurred AND each was followed by domain-specific counter events. Pass to GameSituation. Update prompt to reference burned_axes directly instead of asking the LLM to derive it from recent_doctrines.
close_reason: Two-part fix: (1) widened recent_doctrines window from 8 to 16 entries so the LLM can see longer history when reasoning about pivots. (2) Added persistent burned_axes list computed in Go from the FULL doctrine history + persisted stress events. Detection: an axis is burned when it was the dominant weight (>=0.55) in 2+ historical doctrines AND each of those doctrines was followed within 1500 ticks by a domain-specific counter event (aircraft/SAM/Flak for air, infantry/flame/tesla for infantry, army_devastated for vehicle). burned_axes is passed in GameSituation; updated BURNED AXIS prompt rule to treat it as a hard constraint (axis weight <= 0.25) for the rest of the match. baml_src/doctrine.baml + agent/strategist.go.

title: Opener doctrine ignores vs-opponent cautionaries warning about base-defense failures
description:
Game 20 (france vs russia, 29k ticks lost) opener: aggression=0.80, ground_def=0.35. The librarian surfaced 4 vs-russia cautionaries explicitly citing 'low ground_def + base raids + critical_building_lost' as the recurring failure mode. The LLM still chose a soft-defense opener and got punished by tick 16510 (critical building lost).

Same pattern across games: cautionaries describe shape failures, but the LLM treats them as advisory and the OPENING doctrine doesn't reflect them. By the time gd ramps up via reactive evals, the damage is done.

Fix should be CAUTIONARY-RESPONSIVE, not a hardcoded default — many directives shouldn't open with high gd. Add a prompt rule: when cautionaries reference base-raid failure modes AND we're in early game (situation.tick low or phase == 'Early Game'), the opener must include ground_defense_priority >= 0.6 and economy_priority >= 0.6 regardless of directive aggression. This way only directives facing relevant cautionaries get the bias.
close_reason: Added CAUTIONARY-AWARE OPENER prompt rule. Fires only on the opening doctrine (situation.tick small AND recent_doctrines effectively empty) AND only when cautionary_patterns specifically warn about base raids / harvester harassment / critical_building_lost / low ground_def. When all conditions hold, opener must set ground_defense_priority >= 0.6 AND economy_priority >= 0.6 regardless of directive aggression. Not a default — only kicks in when surfaced cautionaries match the failure mode. baml_src/doctrine.baml line 286.

title: Attack squads target enemy units instead of pressing buildings — high score but no win condition progress
description:
Game 19 (france vs russia, 94k ticks, lost): Vimy ended with HIGHER unit-kill score than the enemy but lost because critical buildings were destroyed faster than Vimy could destroy enemy structures. squad-attack-known-base fired only 14 times across 94k ticks; squad-attack (which targets nearest unit) only 6.

Vimy is excellent at trading units (21 STRONG-rated doctrines, attack > defense ratio) but doesn't convert offensive pressure into building destruction. Enemy structures stay up while units die in the field; eventually enemy lays enough damage on Vimy's CY/refineries to win.

Fix direction: when an attack squad is committed and ground/air targets are visible at the enemy base, prefer high-value structures (construction_yard, war_factory, refinery, tech_center, missile_silo, iron_curtain, naval_yard, airfield) over the nearest unit. The current BestGroundTarget()/BestAirTarget() likely returns proximity-weighted targets — needs value-weighted scoring.
close_reason: BestGroundTarget / BestAirTarget rebalanced: ConstructionYard value bumped to 12 (highest, win-condition target), Refinery bumped to 7 (ground) / 6 (air). Ground distance decay softened from 1/dist to 1/(1 + dist/50) so high-value buildings pull squads even from across the map instead of being out-scored by nearby trash mobile units. Effect: once active defenses are cleared, squads now press CY and infrastructure rather than chasing the closest infantry. rules/env.go + test update.

title: Idle harvesters get stuck — return-idle-harvesters re-issues orders every tick
description:
Live observation: 3 harvesters sitting idle near refineries despite return-idle-harvesters being a low-priority always-on rule. Same command-spam pattern that bit attack/move/scout earlier (vimy fixed via per-actor throttle).

Two issues in ActionSendIdleHarvesters:
1. No throttle: every IdleHarvesters() entry gets a fresh TypeHarvest order each evaluation. If a harvester is momentarily idle (e.g., waiting to dock at refinery, between unload and next harvest), the new order cancels its in-flight activity.
2. Always sends to the FIRST refinery's coordinates. Multiple harvesters converge on one refinery instead of spreading across all of them — visible in screenshot as 3 harvesters parked at same refinery while others sit empty.

Fix: per-actor harvestSent map (Tick + dest) with ~120-tick resend throttle, and round-robin or distance-based refinery selection so harvesters spread out.
close_reason: ActionSendIdleHarvesters now: (1) throttles per-harvester resends to harvestResend=120 ticks via state map, deduping on (Tick, X, Y); (2) round-robins across all refineries instead of always sending to the first. Same per-actor (Tick, dest) pattern used by sendMove/sendAttack/etc. rules/actions.go.

title: Memory query filters by exact faction, blocking lessons-transfer across same-side factions
description:
Game 17 (france vs ukraine) loaded zero candidates from the librarian. Vimy has played as england/germany (allied) and russia (soviet) but never france — so 'WHERE g.our_faction = @our_faction' returns nothing for france.

France, england, and germany share the Allied tech tree (same units, same buildings, similar tactics). Russia and Ukraine share the Soviet tech tree. Lessons within a side should transfer, just not across sides (Soviet APC ≠ Allied Ranger, Iron Curtain ≠ Chronosphere).

Fix: map faction to side (allied: france/england/germany; soviet: russia/ukraine) and change QueryExemplarDoctrines / QueryCautionaryDoctrines / QueryLessons to filter on faction IN (same-side list) instead of strict equality. Cross-side leakage stays blocked.
close_reason: Memory queries now match any same-side faction. Added store.SameSideFactions helper (allied: france/england/germany; soviet: russia/ukraine). Updated QueryExemplarDoctrines, QueryCautionaryDoctrines, QueryLessons SQL to use IN (sqlc.slice('our_factions')). Cross-side leakage stays blocked (Allied vs Soviet differ on units like APC/Ranger and Iron Curtain/Chronosphere). store/queries.sql, store/store.go.

title: Capture pipeline rules orphan engineers when capture_priority drops below 0.1 between doctrines
description:
Game 16 (germany vs ukraine, 72min loss): produce-engineer fired 4 times but capture-building only 1, deliver-apc-to-target 0. Most doctrines had capture_priority=0.00 even though oil refineries were visible (vimy-b2c capturables_visible field is being passed but the LLM keeps dropping the priority).

Architectural gap: the capture pipeline rules (capture-building, produce-engineer, produce-apc, load-engineer-into-apc, deliver-apc-to-target) are only compiled when c.d.CapturePriority > DoctrineEnabled (0.1). When the LLM raises capture_priority briefly to produce an engineer, then drops it back to 0, the capture rules vanish from the rule set on the next doctrine swap. Pre-built engineers and transports stay in the world but no rule directs them — they orphan.

Fix: keep the capture pipeline rules emitted whenever RoleCount('engineer') > 0 OR TransportCount > 0 (i.e., we have units that could capture), independent of CapturePriority. CapturePriority only gates produce-engineer / produce-apc — the directing rules (load, deliver, capture) should always be available.
close_reason: Direction rules (capture-building, load-engineer-into-apc, deliver-apc-to-target) now always emitted regardless of CapturePriority. Production rules (produce-engineer, produce-apc, produce-capture-defense-infantry) still gated on CapturePriority > DoctrineEnabled. Engineers/APCs that outlive a capture_priority drop now have rules to direct them. rules/compiler_core.go + rules/compiler_test.go.

title: Defense squad pre-positions units even when no threat, starving attack formation
description:
Live observation game 16: visible idle force (mammoth tank + 2-3 medium/light tanks) sitting near base, not attacking despite no nearby enemy. Same root cause as vimy-a8e but on the defense side: form-defense-squad fires whenever GroundDefensePriority > 0.3 and idle units exist, pulling 2-5 units into a 'defend' squad. squad-defend-base only fires on BaseUnderAttack — otherwise the defense squad sits idle.

When total ground force is small (post-attrition or early game), defense squad eats the only available units and form-ground-attack starves below its 60%-of-size threshold. Attack never forms, units never act.

Fix: form-defense-squad should only fire when (a) BaseUnderAttack OR (b) there are enough unassigned units to also feed form-ground-attack at its threshold. Otherwise units stay unassigned and flow to attack.
close_reason: form-defense-squad now requires either BaseUnderAttack OR len(UnassignedIdleGround) >= defenseSize + formGroundAttackThreshold. With small armies, units stay unassigned and flow to form-ground-attack instead of being poached into an idle defense squad. When base actually comes under attack, defense squad forms immediately as before. rules/compiler_combat.go.

title: form-ground-attack waits for full GroundAttackGroupSize before forming squad — never attacks with partial force
description:
Game 15: form-defense-squad fired 153 times, form-ground-attack only 63. squad-attack-known-base only 34 commits across a 3-hour match. User observed visible decent force sizes (8-12 units) sitting idle while no attack formed.

Root cause: form-ground-attack condition requires len(UnassignedIdleGround()) >= GroundAttackGroupSize (typically 10). LLM defaults GroundAttackGroupSize to 10 in over half of doctrines. Defense squad takes 2-5 units first (higher priority). If total ground force is <15 units (very common after attrition), only 3-5 are unassigned, well below the 10-unit creation threshold. Squad never spawns, attack never happens.

Fix: form-ground-attack should accept a partial roster — at least 60% of requested size, floor 3. SquadReadyRatio >= 0.6 already gates the actual attack commit, so the squad just needs to exist. Once formed, attrition+reinforcement handles the rest.
close_reason: Lowered form-ground-attack / form-air-attack / form-naval-attack squad-creation thresholds to max(3 or 2, requested_size * 0.6). The full GroundAttackGroupSize still gates SquadReadyRatio for the actual attack commit, but the squad now spawns with a partial roster instead of waiting for the full count. Game 15 had attack squads sitting unformed because LLM defaulted size=10 while only 5-8 were ever simultaneously idle post-defense-poaching. rules/compiler_combat.go.

title: Pivot oscillation: LLM flips between two modes every 1-2 evals
description:
Game 14 (england cold start, 1h45m loss): STICKY PIVOT rule succeeds at preventing revert-to-directive but doesn't catch A→B→A→B oscillation. Doctrine timeline shows infantry-anchor (inf=0.60) and vehicle-siege (veh=0.60) flipping every 1-2 evaluations. Each flip technically satisfies STICKY PIVOT (it IS a pivot from the previous shape), but the cumulative effect is incoherent force composition — army devastated at tick 27220 (62% loss in one engagement) is the downstream cost.

Fix: add prompt rule detecting 3+ shape switches across the last 4-5 doctrines (A→B→A pattern). Once detected, the LLM must commit to ONE of the modes for at least 3 evals regardless of fresh counter events — oscillation is worse than picking the wrong mode and sustaining it.
close_reason: Added ANTI-OSCILLATION rule to doctrine.baml prompt: detects A→B→A→B alternation across last 4 doctrines and requires committing to one mode for 3+ evals before any further pivot. Picks the cheaper/faster-to-mass mode or one that matches current Units/Buildings. Forbids breaking the cycle by introducing a third shape. baml_src/doctrine.baml line 287.

title: War factory must build before naval yard / airfield regardless of doctrine
description:
Game 13 (russia vs germany, naval directive, 19min loss) showed: opening doctrine had nav=0.70 veh=0.35, giving build-naval-yard priority ~650 vs build-war-factory ~633. Naval yard won the slot, war factory never built, ground rush hit at tick 5700, zero produce-vehicle/heavy-vehicle/siege-vehicle firings across the rest of the game.

Vehicles are universally useful — harvesters, defenders, MCV recovery, V2s, APCs for engineer rushes. Naval and air are map-conditional. War factory must ALWAYS come before specialized production yards.

Fix: rules/compiler_buildings.go — when NavalWeight > DoctrineEnabled or AirWeight > DoctrineEnabled, warFactoryPriority floored at 685 (above the 680 ceiling on both build-naval-yard and build-airfield).
close_reason: Floored build-war-factory priority at 685 (above the 680 ceiling on build-naval-yard and build-airfield) whenever either alternative compiles. War factory now wins the build slot first regardless of doctrine weighting. rules/compiler_buildings.go:99

title: Convergence-break pivot is one-shot, LLM reverts on next evaluation
description:
Observed game 11 (russia vs england, naval directive, lost): after critical_building_lost at tick 17620, convergence break fired and doctrine at tick 20230 pivoted correctly (veh=0.60 nav=0.25 gd=0.80). But the very next evaluation (20790) reverted to nav=0.55, and subsequent doctrines kept naval 0.55-0.70. The directive re-anchors every eval because the prompt treats the break as a one-shot.

Fix direction: make the pivot sticky. When a prior pivot is detected in recent_doctrines AND counter events are still present in recent_events, the LLM must maintain the pivoted shape. Add explicit prompt rule: 'if you see in recent_doctrines that you recently pivoted (dominant axis changed substantially) AND counter-events are still firing, the pivot has not yet resolved — maintain it rather than reverting to the directive's preferred shape.'
notes: Initial prompt-only fix didn't hold — game 12 showed pivot at tick 8900 reverted at 9470. Root cause: events feed gets cleared per evaluation, so the LLM saw zero counter events at 9470 and inferred 'situation resolved'. Added persistent stress-event buffer in agent/strategist.go: high-impact events (harvester_lost/under_attack, critical_building_lost, army_devastated, economy_crisis, strategy_countered) stay in the situation feed for 1500 ticks (~3 evals) after firing, deduped by (Kind, Tick). Now the STICKY PIVOT prompt rule actually has the data it needs to evaluate.
close_reason: Added STICKY PIVOT rule to doctrine.baml prompt: once a pivot is detected in recent_doctrines and counter-events are still present, the pivoted shape must be maintained (old dominant axis <= 0.30, new emphasis > 0.5) rather than reverting to directive preference. Only revert after 2-3 consecutive clean evaluations.

title: Strategist doesn't see discovered capturable neutrals (oil derricks etc.)
description:
Observed live: 3 oil refineries visible on the map but capture_priority stayed at 0.05. Root cause: model.GameState.Capturables is populated and used by rule-engine capture actions, but agent.buildSituation does not forward it to GameSituation / the LLM prompt. The strategist has no visibility into discovered neutral tech and therefore no signal to raise capture_priority.

Fix: add a capturables summary (type + count + nearest distance, or positions) to GameSituation and surface in the doctrine prompt. Pair with a consideration note so the LLM knows capture_priority >= 0.3 is needed for engineer+transport to actually grab them.
close_reason: Added capturables_visible TypeCount[] field to GameSituation, populated from GameState.Capturables in buildSituation with counts by type code (oilb/fcom/miss/hosp/etc.). Prompt includes inline hint: 'raise capture_priority >= 0.3 to build engineers to take them'. Won't affect running game until sidecar restart.

title: Missile sub / advanced ship starved by generic produce-ship (same pattern as siege fix)
description:
Observed live game 11 (russia vs france naval directive): subs produced but no missile subs despite tech_priority=0.8 and missile_sub listed #2 in PreferredNaval.

Root cause — same as vimy-erh (vehicle siege):
- produce-advanced-ship priority 430 loses to produce-ship at 440 in exclusive Ship queue
- advNavalCap = lerp(1,3, TechPriority * NavalWeight) caps at 1 once naval drops below ~0.5

Fix: when PreferredNaval primary is missile_sub/cruiser/destroyer (or those units appear at position [0] of PreferredNaval), bump produce-advanced-ship priority above produce-ship AND expand the cap similar to the siege fix (lerp(3,8,...)).
close_reason: Mirrored the vimy-erh siege fix for naval: when PreferredNaval[0] is missile_sub/cruiser/destroyer, produce-advanced-ship priority bumps from 430 to 445 (above produce-ship at 440) and cap expands from lerp(1,3, tech*naval) to lerp(3,8,naval). rules/compiler_production.go:409

title: War factory egress blocked by parked unit stalls vehicle production
description:
Observed live: a ready vehicle in the war factory queue cannot exit because a friendly unit is parked on the egress tile. Production stays stuck indefinitely — queue shows 'ready' but no unit emerges, and all downstream vehicle rules hang.

Fix direction: detect 'vehicle queue stuck in ready state for > N ticks' and nudge any friendly unit within ~2 cells of the war factory rally point away. Similar logic likely needed for barracks (though infantry are smaller and rarely block).
close_reason: Added ActionUnblockWarFactoryEgress + rule unblock-war-factory-egress (priority 892, category vehicle_maintenance). Fires when Vehicle queue has item at 100% and a war factory exists. Nudges the nearest non-harvester, non-MCV ground unit within 3 cells of the war factory ~6 cells along the factory-to-centroid axis. Throttled per actor (120 ticks). rules/actions.go + rules/compiler_core.go.

title: Siege vehicle production starved by flak_truck in vehicle queue
description:
Game 9: v2_launcher was primary preferred_vehicle across most of the match with AirDef often 0.7+. Rule firings show produce-siege-vehicle fired only 14 times vs produce-flak-truck 85 times in 4.7h. Both rules are in the exclusive vehicle queue; flak is cheaper so it keeps winning the cash window, and V2s barely get built even when doctrine says they're the plan.

Fix idea: when PreferredVehicle[0] is a siege unit (v2_launcher / artillery), produce-siege-vehicle priority should exceed produce-flak-truck, or flak production should be capped once a minimum flak count is reached so siege gets cash room. Needs investigation in rules/compiler_production.go.
close_reason: Bumped siege cap to lerp(3,8,VehicleWeight) when PreferredVehicle[0] is v2_launcher/artillery. Prior default cap (1-3) let produce-flak-truck snipe every vehicle-queue window after hitting cap. rules/compiler_production.go:286

title: Strategist ignores cautionary lessons when directive is strongly themed
description:
Game 9 ran 4h42m (282k ticks) and produced 341 doctrines, ~300 of them Air Supremacy / Skyhammer variants with air_weight 0.55-0.85. Nearly every one was rated 'weak' by the librarian, and 5 explicit lessons in the feed said 'cut air, raise ground_def, protect economy'. The LLM kept retrying air-heavy shapes anyway — the directive ('total air dominance') anchored harder than the cautionaries.

Needed: when repeat 'weak' ratings appear on doctrines matching an active lesson's trigger, treat it as a mandatory pivot signal (e.g. force a divergent axis for the next N doctrines, or escalate lesson weight in the prompt). This should override directive theming.
close_reason: Added RecentDoctrine class + situation.recent_doctrines field (last 8 in-game doctrines as shape fingerprints), passed to GenerateDoctrine prompt. Added CONVERGENCE BREAK rule requiring a structurally different dominant axis when 4+ recent doctrines converge AND counter-events are present. baml_src/doctrine.baml + agent/strategist.go recentDoctrineSummaries.

title: Route ActionEmergencyDefendBase through sendAttackMove — spam was missed in vimy-34z
description: 3-hour stalemate log shows dozens of consecutive 'emergency base defense — recalling nearby units' messages (target IDs churning 3433→3505→3509 etc.) every tick during combat. ActionEmergencyDefendBase sends TypeAttackMove directly each fire without going through the sendAttackMove throttle added in vimy-34z. Result: 14 nearby units get their AttackMove cancelled every tick, they thrash in place instead of engaging, and they're unavailable for offensive squads (which keep forming, getting recalled, re-forming).\n\nOne-line fix: replace the direct conn.Send(TypeAttackMove, …) in ActionEmergencyDefendBase with sendAttackMove(env, conn, ids, enemy.X, enemy.Y). The throttle will suppress identical resends within attackMoveResend ticks, letting defenders actually close with the target.
close_reason: ActionEmergencyDefendBase routed through sendAttackMove. The per-actor throttle (attackMoveResend = 60 ticks) will suppress identical recall orders so defenders actually close with the target instead of thrashing. Full test suite already green — sendAttackMove has existing test coverage from vimy-34z.

title: Throttle squad Attack + AttackMove orders — 5556 AttackMove spam stalls combat force
description:
Squad combat actions (SquadFocusFire via TypeAttack, SquadAttackMove via TypeAttackMove, plus SquadAttackKnownBase, SquadReengage, SquadDefend, SquadAirStrike, etc.) re-issue fresh commands every tick they fire. Live game: 5556 attack_move commands in a single match, 52 identical Attack(actor→target) resends per squad member across 7 members targeting one unit. Each resend cancels the in-flight attack activity and restarts pathing, so the combat force stalls mid-map never reaching its target. Then when orders finally stop the units go idle and scout-with-idle-units picks them up → they go explore instead of finishing the attack. Classic command-spam pattern we've already fixed for Move (APC, scout patrol) and Capture.

Fix: apply the same throttle pattern to squad Attack and AttackMove sends. Per-actor maps in engine memory, configurable resend window (~60 ticks), skip identical resends within window. Apply to at minimum SquadFocusFire and SquadAttackMove — these are the top offenders per the firing counts. Follow-up beads can cover SquadAirStrike / SquadReengage / SquadAttackKnownBase / SquadDefend.
close_reason: Added sendAttack (TypeAttack) and sendAttackMove (TypeAttackMove) throttle helpers with 60-tick resend windows. Applied to SquadFocusFire, SquadAirStrike, SquadAttackMove, and SquadAttackKnownBase. For SquadAttackKnownBase: added attackMoveHasFreshTarget probe so the 16-step hunt cycle advances only when a send will actually land — without it, the step counter rotated through all 16 points once per tick and units never reached any of them. Tests cover throttle suppression, target-change bypass, mixed-batch partial suppression, and the fresh-target probe.

title: Throttle + stall-advance for ActionScoutWithIdleUnits — 772 attack_move spam
description:
ActionScoutWithIdleUnits advances scoutWaypointIdx unconditionally every tick and sends a fresh AttackMove to the top-2 idle ground units. Each re-send cancels the in-flight attack-move activity in OpenRA, so the cleanup force gets pulled into a new map corner every tick and never forms up or arrives. Live game: 772 attack_move commands, actors seen bouncing around 5 waypoints with no real progress. Combined with Scout 0.60 doctrine weight, this burns the tank/rocket cleanup crew through scouting cycles they can't complete.

Fix: mirror the scout-patrol rework — per-actor round-robin state in memory['idleScoutMoveSent'], stall tracking in memory['idleScoutProgress'] (using actorStalledAt), throttle with scoutMoveResend, rotate waypoint only on arrive OR stall. Preserve the 'up to 2 units' cap.
close_reason: ActionScoutWithIdleUnits rewritten to use the same per-actor patrol machinery as ActionScoutPatrol: persistent round-robin waypoint assignment in memory['idleScoutMoveSent'], stall-tracking in memory['idleScoutProgress'] (scoutStallTicks=200), scoutMoveResend throttle. 'Up to 2 units' cap preserved; each selected unit now gets its own AttackMove rather than one batched command. Test covers throttle suppression + stall-triggered idx advance.

title: ActionScoutPatrol: add stall-advance so unreachable waypoints don't trap scouts
description:
Dog produced, scouted to center (64,64), then received 93 Move(5,5) commands from (64,64) over ~3700 ticks without moving a single cell. Waypoint (5,5) was unreachable (likely chokepoint or terrain lock). Throttle prevented spam but there's no stall-escape: once assigned an unreachable waypoint, dog stuck for the whole game.

Mirror the APC-scout fix (vimy-qmm): if the scout hasn't moved in ~200 ticks while assigned to its current waypoint, force-advance idx to the next in rotation. Same threshold as apcScoutStallTicks. Refactor apcStalledFor into a shared actorStalledAt helper keyed by memory slot so APC-delivery and ground-scout stall tracking don't collide.
close_reason: ActionScoutPatrol now calls scoutStalled (actorStalledAt with 'scoutProgress' key, scoutStallTicks=200) before computing waypoint idx. On stall, forceAdvance triggers nextPatrolIdx to rotate to the next waypoint and stall tracking is cleared. apcStalledFor refactored to call shared actorStalledAt helper. Test simulates the live scenario: dog at (64,64) stuck on assigned (5,5) for 250 ticks → idx advances from 1 to 2.

title: APC scout uses round-robin patrol like ActionScoutPatrol
description:
Live game showed APCs in scout mode only visited 4 of 9 map waypoints — specifically the 3 far corners + top-mid, never the 4 mid-edge points or the center. Farthest-from-current-position pick oscillates between opposite corners; mid-edges are never 'farthest' from anywhere on that oscillation path, so enemy bases along map edges never get sighted.

User wants APC scout mode to behave exactly like the dedicated scout patrol (ActionScoutPatrol) — round-robin through all 9 waypoints, advance on arrival. Only switch to delivery mode when a capturable/enemy structure becomes visible (which is already how the action's top-level branching works).

Plan:
- Extract a shared nextPatrolTarget helper that round-robins waypoints, advances on arrival-within-radius or forced (stall/TTL).
- Use it from both ActionScoutPatrol and the explore branches of ActionUnloadAPCNearTarget + ActionDeliverAssaultAPC.
- Add Idx field to apcExploreEntry for round-robin state.
- Drop pickAPCExploreWaypoint and its skipX/skipY special-case — round-robin makes it unnecessary.
- Update the existing stalled-waypoint test to assert round-robin advance behavior.
close_reason: APC scout mode now mirrors ActionScoutPatrol exactly. New nextPatrolIdx + takePatrolPoolIdx helpers shared between both paths (same round-robin advance-on-arrival semantics). advanceAPCPatrol wraps them for APC explore, keeping APC-specific concerns (TTL, stall-advance). pickAPCExploreWaypoint and its skipX/skipY hack deleted. apcExploreEntry gained Idx (round-robin state). Tests: round-robin visits all 9 waypoints from a corner-base scenario (the live-game bug); sticky preserves idx+AssignedAt when APC hasn't arrived; stall advances idx.

title: APC scout waypoint stuck on unreachable corner - deterministic farthest pick
description:
Observed live at ~7:39 game time: engineer-loaded APC 281 issued 140 Move commands in 7 minutes, all to (123,123). Actor moved only from (27,38) -> (30,37). Throttle is not the problem — it correctly sends one Move per 60 ticks. The problem is the destination is unreachable and the re-pick logic deterministically returns the same bad waypoint.

Two bugs in actions.go:
1. pickAPCExploreWaypoint uses farthest-from-current-position. A stuck APC at (27,38) will always re-pick (123,123) because no position changes. Every apcExploreTTL (600 ticks) expiry produces the identical choice.
2. The explore branch of ActionUnloadAPCNearTarget has no stall detection — apcIsStalled only runs in the target != nil branch. A scout stuck at its current position never triggers a re-pick, unload, or alternate destination.

Fix:
- When re-picking, exclude the previous waypoint from the candidate set (or mark waypoints that the APC has been trying to reach for > K ticks without progress as 'bad' for that APC).
- Add explore-mode stall detection: if apcDeliveryProgress shows the APC hasn't moved meaningfully in ~200 ticks while a scout target is assigned, immediately pick a new waypoint (skipping the stuck one) rather than waiting for TTL.

Also: consider whether generateWaypoints should pre-filter for pathable terrain (env.Terrain is available). A waypoint on water/cliff will never be reachable by a ground APC.
close_reason: Added apcScoutStalled() check in the explore branches of both ActionUnloadAPCNearTarget and ActionDeliverAssaultAPC. When a scouting APC hasn't moved in 200 ticks (~8s), force an immediate re-pick. pickAPCExploreWaypoint gained skipX/skipY params so the stall-triggered re-pick excludes the unreachable waypoint — farthest-first heuristic no longer locks onto the same bad corner. Test covers the live scenario (APC at 27,38 with stale target at 123,123 → must re-pick a different waypoint).

title: Throttle Capture commands - spam cancels capture activity like Move spam
description:
Engineer 492 was issued 'capture target 651' 111 times and 'capture target 619' 111 times in the same game. Engineer 496 got 56/34/22/17/13/10 captures across 6 different targets. Total 552 capture commands across the 38-minute game.

Root cause: same as the Move spam we just fixed. ActionCaptureBuilding re-issues a fresh Capture order every tick the rule fires. In OpenRA, each new order replaces the current activity, so the engineer resets its 'walk to target' every tick and never arrives to actually capture. capture-building fire count in rule_firings looks healthy (555 total) but zero captures complete.

Fix mirrors sendAPCMove:
- Track (engineerID, targetID, tick) in memory['captureSent'] map.
- Skip re-send if same pair within ~60 ticks.
- Clear on engineer death / target death / target capture (or just let pruning by 'unknown actor' happen on the C# side).

Extend actions.go:ActionCaptureBuilding to route through a new sendCaptureOrder helper.
close_reason: Added captureOrderResend throttle (60 ticks) mirroring sendAPCMove fix. ActionCaptureBuilding now tracks last (engineer,target,tick) in memory['captureSent'] and skips resends of an identical order within the window. Target-change or window-expiry triggers a fresh send. Test covers seed / suppression / window-expiry resend / target-change resend.

title: Throttle APC Move commands - spam pins APC in place
description:
Watching a live game, user saw APC never moved despite deliver-apc-to-target firing 473 times. Debug log shows 473 Move(123,123) commands for actor 278, with the APC moving only 14 cells total (27,38)->(37,34) across the entire game.

Root cause: ActionUnloadAPCNearTarget and ActionDeliverAssaultAPC unconditionally issue a Move command every tick their condition holds. In OpenRA, a new Move order cancels the current activity, so each tick the APC restarts pathfinding and barely progresses.

Same pattern as the flee-harvesters spam bug (fixed via harvesterFleeing state + harvesterFleeResend=100 throttle). Apply the same throttle to APC deliveries: track last-sent (actor, dest, tick) and skip re-send if destination unchanged within N ticks.

Fix in vimy-core/rules/actions.go:
- Add apcMoveEntry + getAPCMoveState + maybeSendAPCMove helpers
- Route all Move sends in ActionUnloadAPCNearTarget and ActionDeliverAssaultAPC through maybeSendAPCMove
- Clear apcMoveSent on unload (extend clearAPCTracking)
- Resend window: ~60 ticks (faster than harvesters since capturable targets can shift)

Tests: extend transport_test/actions_test to assert second same-tick call within window does NOT send a new Move but that a destination change or stale-window expiry does.
close_reason: Added apcMoveSent throttle (60-tick resend window) mirroring the flee-harvesters fix. All 4 Move sends in ActionUnloadAPCNearTarget and ActionDeliverAssaultAPC now go through sendAPCMove. Cleared on unload via clearAPCTracking. Test asserts first call seeds, second within window is suppressed, third past window resends.

title: APC stall threshold too aggressive: premature unload at base
description: Stall threshold was 50 ticks (~2s). OpenRA pathfinding can take longer to start when Move is queued behind Enter orders or adjacent cells are blocked. Premature stall fired while APC was still at base → Unload command dumped engineer in place → engineer walked on foot across map and died. Evidence from traced game: deliver-apc-to-target fired 154 times between ticks 14040-16700 then stopped; capture-building continued firing through 27000+ (idle engineers on foot). Bumped threshold to 400 ticks (~16s). Added TestActionUnloadAPCNearTarget_DoesNotStallPrematurely to lock in the invariant.
close_reason: Fixed: apcStallTicks 50 → 400 in actions.go. Added premature-stall regression test. Full suite green.

title: Combat-loaded APCs stranded when no building intel
description: Trace of game 1776653606 (russia, loss) showed load-assault-infantry 55 fires vs deliver-assault-apc 0 fires. Root cause: HasEnemyIntel() requires FromBuildings=true (updateIntel in env.go:1413). When the enemy attacked with units only and scouts never sighted buildings, the gate stayed false and combat-loaded APCs sat at base. Fix: ActionDeliverAssaultAPC now falls back to scout-with-APC (same pattern as engineer path) when no land target exists. deliver-assault-apc rule drops HasEnemyIntel() gate when TransportAssault >= DoctrineSignificant. 1 new action test + 2 compiler subtests.
close_reason: Fixed in rules/actions.go + rules/compiler_core.go. Aggressive TransportAssault drops HasEnemyIntel() gate. ActionDeliverAssaultAPC scouts when no land target exists. Full suite green.

title: APC cargo intent pruned during load-in-flight transient
description: Even with HasEnemyIntel() true, loaded APCs sat idle. Root cause: pruneAPCCargoIntent deleted any tag where CargoCount=0. Loads take a tick or two for the server to register the Enter command; during that window the APC is tagged but still shows CargoCount=0, so the prune destroyed the tag. When CargoCount finally incremented, the APC was tagless and both deliver rules skipped it. Fix: prune only removes tags for dead APCs. Tag is explicitly cleared on unload (both engineer and combat paths) via clearAPCTracking/ClearAPCCargoIntent. 2 new tests + 1 updated.
close_reason: Fixed: prune only removes dead APCs; tags cleared explicitly on unload via clearAPCTracking. TestAPCCargoIntent_PrunesStaleTags updated, TestAPCCargoIntent_ClearedOnUnload and TestAPCCargoIntent_ClearedOnAssaultUnload added. Full suite green.

title: APC cargo intent race: combat load overwrote engineer tag on same tick
description: load-engineer-into-apc (845) and load-assault-infantry (838) both target IdleEmptyAPCs()[0] in the same tick. Priority ordering runs engineer first (tags 'engineer'), then combat overwrites to 'combat'. The APC ends up holding an engineer but tagged combat, so deliver-apc-to-target skips it and deliver-assault-apc won't fire until HasEnemyIntel() — APCs sit idle. Fixed by making engineer tag sticky in ActionLoadCombatInfantry: only write combat tag if APC isn't already tagged engineer. 1 new test (TestLoadCombatInfantry_DoesNotOverwriteEngineerTag).
close_reason: Fixed in rules/actions.go: engineer tag is sticky in ActionLoadCombatInfantry. Test TestLoadCombatInfantry_DoesNotOverwriteEngineerTag covers the race. Full suite green.

title: Game 106: infantry-reserves hold was unreachable, and never released in the win either
description:
Game 106 (england vs ukraine, 39260 ticks, loss). Armour 5, infantry 18, fielded 23 — against game 104's 8/38/46 and the game 105 win's 9/31/40.

Replaying the post-war-factory states:
  old infantry bar (380)  reachable 49%
  NEW infantry bar (900)  reachable  8%
  tank bar (800)          reachable 12%
  peak combat-vehicle-count: 4, against an escape of 15.

So the hold introduced in vimy-tbe never released. Nor did it in game 105 — escape 13 there against a peak of 9. The win happened WITH the hold permanently on, which means the win does not validate the threshold, only the direction.

Root cause: the escape was half of army-cap(), and army-cap is multiplied by force_size (2.2x at 0.8). Vimy fields 4-9 combat vehicles because vehicle production is cash- and queue-bound — cash >= 800 holds ~12-13% of states and the Vehicle queue is busy ~61% — so any escape above about 4 is permanent by construction. force_size answers 'how large an army to keep'; borrowing it for 'when do we stop saving for the first tanks' is what put the number out of reach.

Fix (f72f530): escape is now lerp(2, 5, vehicle-weight), which is 4 across every doctrine observed and not force_size scaled. Protects the climb from zero to four vehicles, which is the part that was genuinely broken — Vimy could not get past one to three tanks because rifles cleared 380 and tanks needed 800.

Expected cost, stated up front: armour peak may settle nearer 5-7 than game 105's 9, because past four vehicles infantry competes for cash again. That is deliberate. The previous value was not a stricter version of this, it was an accidental permanent tax.

Confounder worth keeping in view: game 106's strategist chose infantry_weight 0.15 against 0.25 in games 104 and 105, so the screen was thin before this clause thinned it. The clause and the doctrine compounded; neither alone explains 23 fielded.

Not yet measured in a game.

title: The safe approach axis is chosen once and never reconsidered
description:
User observation, game 106: the enemy chokes one entry with defenses while other approaches stay open, and Vimy does not exploit it — 'something I thought we tried to address a while back'.

It was addressed, but only for the first approach. SquadAttackKnownBase (actions.go) consults BestApproachAxis inside 'if state.Step == 0'. state.Step resets to 0 only when the target base COORDINATES change, and increments after every send. So a squad picks a threat-avoiding entry once per base and then attacks the centroid directly for the rest of the match — through attacks, disengages and re-attacks. Game 105 had 34 squad-attack-known-base firings and 5 disengages against one base: one informed approach, dozens of blind ones.

Two further limits on the same path:
- ThreatField is built from getEnemyDefenses(e.Memory), i.e. only defenses Vimy has SEEN. An unscouted base looks open.
- bestApproachAxisWithField returns early when directScore < openEnoughThreshold, so a base with little remembered threat never triggers a reroute at all.

Correction to the premise in that particular screenshot: the defenses visible were AA guns, and defenseThreatWeight already scores AAGun and SAMSite at 0.4 against 1.0-2.5 for pillbox/turret/flame/tesla, precisely because AA cannot shoot ground. For a ground squad that approach is genuinely not choked, so declining to reroute there is correct behaviour. The mechanism is still worth fixing for real ground defenses.

Fix direction: re-evaluate the approach axis when the squad re-commits rather than only on first contact with a base — e.g. reset Step to 0 (or re-run the axis check) when squadAttackState transitions back to Attacking after a disengage, or on some interval. Care needed: the existing comment warns that re-checking mid-fight oscillates ('attack, spread, regroup, attack'), so the trigger should be a fresh commitment, not every tick.

Related: vimy-v8a widened the hunt that runs once the squad arrives; this is the complementary problem of how it gets there.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Nathan Stehr
comments.text: 99e9336 — the hunt step now resets on re-approach (target changed, or committing again after not attacking) as well as on a coordinate change, so BestApproachAxis is consulted each time the squad walks in rather than once per base. Deliberately NOT reset on commitStale: that fires every 2000 ticks of a fight already underway, and the counter it would reset is the outward ring search from vimy-v8a, which has to keep growing to find a razed base — resetting there would have silently undone that fix.

title: produce-spy fires on scout-priority, which is always high — 3-6 spies a game for nothing
description:
produce-spy (production.vy:202) gates on 'capture-priority > 0.2 or scout-priority > 0.3'. Across games 96-100, capture_priority is 0.00 in ALL 167 doctrine windows and scout_priority is 0.60-0.75 in ALL 167. So the capture half never fires and the scout half is unconditionally open — the spy is bought purely as a scout.

role-count(spy) < 1 caps the live count at 1, but spies die and get rebuilt: acted 3,2,3,4,3,6 in games 96-101 (6 in game 101). Spy costs 500. That is ~1500-3000 credits a game on a unit roles.go:470 lists in nonCombatUnits and roles.go:468 describes as 'a spy less than nothing' in a fight — under a directive that says 'Use aircraft for scouting and support only'.

Not displacing rifles: produce-spy is priority 438, below infantry-base() (490/500), so it only wins the produce-infantry category when the cheaper infantry rules are themselves blocked. The cost is the credits, not the queue slot.

Proposed fix: drop the scout-priority disjunct, leaving 'require capture-priority > 0.2'. Vimy already has scout-with-idle-units and scout-with-scouts using units it has already paid for. Given capture_priority has been 0.00 in every window of every game, this effectively retires the spy under current directives, which is the intended outcome.

Needs a RETUNED entry (Field::Condition).

title: repair-buildings matches 1300 times and orders nothing, because its cash floor lives in the action
description:
Game 85: repair-buildings matched 1300 times, acted 0. A 100 percent no-op rate, larger than deploy-mcv 336/39.

The rule is:

  rule repair-buildings {
    priority 200
    category maintenance
    do repair-buildings
    require count(damaged-buildings) > 0
  }

ActionRepairDamagedBuildings opens with:

  if env.State.Player.Cash < repairCashFloor { return nil }   // repairCashFloor = 500

Game 85 held cash at 0 for most of its length, so every firing hit that early return.

This is the same shape as the FormSquad bug fixed 2026-09-07: a gate enforced in the action but absent from the rule, so the rule matches constantly, achieves nothing, and inflates its own firing count. It also pollutes the matched/acted signal that Currie now leads its report with — this was the largest no-op in the game and it is a symptom, not a cause.

Fix: add require cash >= 500 to the rule so the condition and the action agree. Needs a RETUNED entry, since Go has no such clause.

Found by Currie leading with the biggest matched/acted gap, on the first render of that feature.

title: Currie's blame ranking is swamped by completion guards
description:
Game 83's report: the top 10 blame sites, all at 96-97 sole per 100 states, are clauses like 'not squad-exists(harvester-guard)', 'not squad-exists(ground-defense)', 'not squad-exists(ground-attack)', 'not squad-exists(air-attack)', 'queue-ready(Building)'.

Every one of them is a rule that ALREADY DID ITS JOB. The squad exists, so the rule that forms it correctly stops. That is success being reported as the single largest cause of failure, and it fills the entire first screen — the real findings (squad-attack's target clause at 59 sole, scout-with-idle-units at 130) are below the fold.

Currie already knows this shape: chain.go has satisfiedByCompletion() for exactly these clauses, and the report even annotates them 'all of them already fire — the sample missed it'. The blame RANKING just doesn't use it.

Fix: exclude clauses matching satisfiedByCompletion from the sole-blame ranking, or demote them to a separate 'guards that are doing their job' section. Same for a site whose rules all have Acted > 0.

This is the third time this class of noise has produced a wrong reading — it is the same failure as the three bad LLM recommendations: a blame count cannot distinguish 'this gate is too tight' from 'this gate is correct and closed'.
close_reason:
Fixed in two passes. Working guards (Live sites, where every rule the line blocks already fires) now rank below lines that actually stopped something. Then a second class appeared behind them: clauses the faction can never satisfy — game 85 was germany and four of its top eight sites were support-power-ready of SovietParatroopers and friends, at 445 sole out of 475 states.

rules.SupportPowerReachable reads the mod prerequisites, and is per-COUNTRY where the mod is: SovietParatroopers needs aircraft.soviet, SovietSpyPlane needs structures.russia, UkraineParabombs needs aircraft.ukraine. A Ukrainian player cannot call the Russian spy plane. Powers absent from the table are treated as reachable — no evidence is not evidence of absence, and calling a merely-idle rule impossible is the error the table exists to prevent.

Curries impossibleFor also checks positively-mentioned roles against BuildableByFaction, skipping negated has-role mentions since never having the thing is what satisfies them.

Both classes are counted rather than silently dropped: the figure now says how many correct lines were ranked below. Game 85: 117.

title: Priority collisions in exclusive categories make rebuild order nondeterministic
description: Found by vimyc's type checker on the first real doctrine it was pointed at. Two pairs of rules share a priority inside an exclusive category, so which one fires is decided by sort.Slice, which Go does not guarantee to be stable.
design:
compileRules sorts with sort.Slice, which is NOT stable. Equal priorities
therefore order arbitrarily, and inside an exclusive category the first one to
fire blocks the rest. So the choice between these is a coin flip that can land
differently between runs of an identical rule set.

  rebuild-airfield / rebuild-naval-yard   priority 800, category rebuild (exclusive)
  build-aa-defense / build-gap-generator  priority 520, category defense (exclusive)

Both rebuild rules are simultaneously eligible on a water map where an airfield
and a naval yard have both been destroyed, the Building queue is free, and cash
is at least 300:

  rebuild-airfield    lost-role(airfield),   not queue-busy(Building), can-build-role(airfield),   cash >= 300
  rebuild-naval-yard  map-has-water, lost-role(naval-yard), not queue-busy(Building), can-build-role(naval-yard), cash >= 300

Two further pairs collide in `micro`, which is not exclusive, so both still fire
and only their relative order is undefined:

  recall-overextended-ground-attack / recall-overextended-naval-attack   405
  squad-disengage-ground-attack / squad-disengage-naval-attack           410

FIXES, either would do:
  - give the colliding rules distinct priorities in compiler_*.go
  - use sort.SliceStable in compileRules, which makes the order source-order
    rather than arbitrary; vimyc already sorts stably for this reason

NOT FIXED NOW: same reasoning as vimy-1h7 — changing bot behaviour while the
rule engine replacement is in flight would confound the comparison.
acceptance_criteria: Colliding priorities resolved, or the sort made stable, and vimyc's check_priority_collisions reports nothing for real doctrines.

title: form-ground-attack re-forms the squad constantly
description: Observed in a real game export: form-ground-attack fired 149 times over 11,300 ticks, and squad-exists(ground-attack) was false at every single firing. Not being fixed yet — the rule engine replacement should land first, or a behaviour change afterwards cannot be attributed.
design:
DATA (~/.vimy/exports/export-20260903-200340.json, 261 sampled states, ticks 50..13050):

  form-ground-attack   evaluated 249, fired 149 (60%)
  at every firing:     squad-exists(ground-attack)        false  (149/149)
                       squad-needs-reinforcement(...)     false  (149/149)
                       unassigned-idle-ground             4..11, median 6
  across all states:   squad-exists(ground-attack)  true in  64/261 (24%)
                       squad-exists(ground-defense) true in 180/261

The rule always fires via the "no squad exists and there are spare units"
branch, never via reinforcement. So it creates a squad and the squad is gone
again by the next sampled evaluation. It accounts for 149 of 174 total firings
in the sample — 86%.

CANDIDATE CAUSES, untested:
  - Engine.Swap deletes Memory["squads"] on every doctrine change. A game with
    frequent swaps would produce exactly this. Cheapest to check first.
  - Units dying or being poached by form-defense-squad; ground-defense exists in
    180/261 states while ground-attack exists in 64.
  - updateSquads pruning squads whose members are gone.

WHY NOT FIXED NOW:
  Changing bot behaviour while building the vimyc rule engine would confound the
  comparison — a squad-behaviour change afterwards could not be attributed to
  either. See vimy-8wk.

USE AS A VALIDATION TARGET:
  This was found by eye from one export. If vimyc's static analysis or
  blocked-on tooling surfaces it independently, that is evidence the tooling
  works. Worth trying before fixing.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified and confirmed against a recorded export. Fix deferred until the vimyc engine is in place.

title: Grow airfield count to match doctrinal aircraft cap by physical pad capacity
description: Game 56 (air doctrine): produce-aircraft 11 firings vs cancel-stuck 10 = 91% cancel ratio, only 5 sorties flew. AircraftCapacity gate (vimy-26i) limited total production attempts but underlying issue: 1 airfield = 4 pads, doctrine wanted 5-6 aircraft, physical capacity was the bottleneck. Old build-extra-airfield gated on RoleCount and doctrinal cap — chicken-and-egg preventing pad expansion. Fix: gate on physical AircraftCapacity < doctrinal cap AND CombatAircraftCount near-full. Also lowered trigger threshold from DoctrineExtreme (0.4) to DoctrineEnabled (0.1) so modest air doctrines can also grow pads. Tests added.
close_reason: Shipped. build-extra-airfield now gates on AircraftCapacity() vs doctrinal cap instead of RoleCount vs static extraCap. Fires when physical pads can't hold the doctrine's aircraft ambition AND existing pads are near-full. Trigger threshold lowered to DoctrineEnabled so modest air doctrines can grow pads too.
