Tests: TestCompileDoctrine_ExtraAirfieldFiresAtAirEnabled (compiles at air_weight=0.2, previously blocked at 0.4) and TestCompileDoctrine_ExtraAirfieldGatesOnPhysicalCapacity (verifies new gate structure). All tests pass.

title: Widen being_rushed tick window to catch slow-tempo rushes
description:
Game 33 (22.6k tick fast loss): first harvester attack at tick 9980 against a still-small base (5 buildings). The rush detection rule had its cutoff at tick 6000, so being_rushed was false and the softer harvester_harassed rule fired instead. The doctrine pivoted to ground_def=0.8 + economy=0.8 (correct response to harassment), but missed the RUSH RESPONSE prompt rule which prescribes a stronger counter-force shape (infantry>=0.5 with rifle/dog spam, aggression 0.4-0.6, capture=0). By the time the harassment response kicked in, vimy had already lost ground; war factory fell at tick 18700.

Fix: bump rushTickCutoff 6000 → 10500 and harassTickFloor 6000 → 10500 (keep them aligned so the two flags stay mutually exclusive). The small-base condition (<=6 buildings) still prevents the rule from firing once vimy has an established base, so the change only affects slow-tempo rushes against an immature base.

Test: TestComputePressureFlags_SlowRushTriggers covers the game-33 scenario (tick 10000, 5 buildings, recent harvester attack → being_rushed=true).
close_reason: Bumped rushTickCutoff 6000→10500 and harassTickFloor 6000→10500 to keep flags mutually exclusive. Small-base condition (<=6 buildings) unchanged, so the rule only catches slow-tempo rushes against immature bases. New test TestComputePressureFlags_SlowRushTriggers covers the game-33 scenario.

title: Air burn recovery window for air-superiority directive fidelity
description:
vimy-jpp made air burn at threshold=1 (single SAM counter), which is appropriate for the typical 'oops a SAM appeared' case but neuters air-superiority directives — once vimy commits an aircraft and a SAM kills it, no more aircraft for the rest of a 100k+ tick match even after vimy SEADs the SAM. Fix: add per-axis recovery window. Air gets 5000-tick recovery; if no air counter event in the last 5000 ticks, axis un-burns. Vehicle/infantry/naval keep persistent burn (counter-tech like Tesla/Flame Tower tends to keep stacking, not get cleared).

Implementation: new burnedAxisRecoveryTicks map (axis -> recovery ticks). computeBurnedAxes now takes currentTick and tracks per-axis latest counter; if recovery > 0 and currentTick - latestCounter > recovery, the axis is un-burned. Factored out shared eventMatchesAxis helper.

Tests: TestComputeBurnedAxes_AirUnburnsAfterRecoveryWindow (air burns then un-burns after 5000 ticks), TestComputeBurnedAxes_VehicleStaysBurnedAcrossMatch (vehicle remains burned for the rest of the match). Existing tests updated to pass currentTick.
close_reason: Implemented: burnedAxisRecoveryTicks map with air=5000. computeBurnedAxes now takes currentTick, tracks latest counter per axis, un-burns when recovery elapsed. eventMatchesAxis factored out. 2 new tests + existing tests updated.

title: Bias defense placement toward threatened refinery during harvester raids
description: Implemented: when CountFleeingHarvesters >= 2, defenseHint shifts placement strategy. (1) Seeds 4 extra candidates per refinery in a small ring (~3 cells out, cardinal offsets). (2) Replaces the normal scoring with a refinery-weighted variant: refineryScore 0.50, spread 0.15, threat 0.15, choke 0.10, perimeter 0.10. The result is that pillboxes / turrets get placed at the refineries being raided rather than on the front-facing perimeter. Without this, defenses cluster around centroid + threat-toward-enemy and refineries on the periphery sit naked. Test TestDefenseHint_HarvesterEmergencyBiasesToRefinery locks in the bias.
close_reason: Implemented as described. defenseHint now detects harvester emergency via CountFleeingHarvesters(memory) >= 2 and switches to a refinery-biased placement: seeds 4 extra candidates per refinery in a tight cardinal ring, replaces score weights with refineryScore 0.50 dominant. Test TestDefenseHint_HarvesterEmergencyBiasesToRefinery covers the bias. All other tests still pass.

title: ApproachWaypoint picks defended-edge path instead of open flank
description:
Live observation: vimy's units repeatedly funnel through the defended south side of an enemy base when the east is wide open. Should obviously route east.

Why the current ApproachWaypoint (rules/env.go:1821) fails to shift entry:
- Single BFS through threat field with per-hot-cell penalty=5 finds the shortest *weighted* path
- When our base is on the same side as the defenses, the shortest weighted path just SKIMS the edge of the defense paint — the extra distance of a wide detour (east-then-north) costs more than the small penalty of grazing the defenses
- Waypoint = last cool cell before first hot cell on that path, so units stage just outside the defense cluster, then walk into it on the next leg
- This is one-shot path optimization. To actually 'enter from a different side', you need to evaluate candidate sides explicitly, not let the BFS pick its own way through

Proposed fix: add BestApproachAxis(destX, destY) — sample 8 compass directions around the target at a fixed approach radius (e.g. 12 cells), score each candidate waypoint by the threat sum in a corridor from our base centroid to that waypoint, return the candidate with lowest corridor threat. Falls back to direct routing when all candidates are equally clean.

Wire into:
- SquadAttackMove (ground) — replace groundApproachWaypointFor's call to env.ApproachWaypoint
- SquadAttackKnownBase (ground+naval) — replace the existing env.ApproachWaypoint call
- SquadAirStrike — air variant using AirThreatField

Acceptance: with defenses clustered on the south side of a target and the east side clear, BestApproachAxis returns a waypoint east of the target, not south. Existing ApproachWaypoint tests still pass (it can remain as a lower-level utility, just no longer the front door for squad routing).
close_reason: Replaced single-BFS ApproachWaypoint with multi-candidate BestApproachAxis as the front door for squad routing. Samples 8 compass-direction waypoints around the target at ~8 zone-cells radius, scores each by threat-sum in the AABB corridor from our base centroid to that candidate, returns the lowest-scoring one. Only returns a waypoint when (a) direct corridor exceeds openEnoughThreshold AND (b) best candidate is ≥20% cleaner than direct (avoids constant re-routing). Wired into groundApproachWaypointFor (SquadAttackMove), SquadAttackKnownBase, and airApproachWaypointFor (SquadAirStrike). ApproachWaypoint retained as lower-level utility; existing tests still pass. New tests: TestBestApproachAxis_PicksOpenFlank verifies that defenses south of a target push the waypoint north/east; TestBestApproachAxis_OpenCorridorReturnsNoWaypoint verifies no detour fires when corridor is clean.

title: Route attacks via threat-aware approach waypoint when target visible
description:
Observation (game vs Soviet turtle): the bot AI clusters base defenses on one side and leaves other entries open. Vimy's aircraft fly straight-line over the AA cluster every time and die; ground/vehicles do the same against pillbox/tesla clusters. They could shift entry by a small offset and take the base.

Existing infra in rules/env.go: ApproachWaypoint(destX, destY) → returns a staging zone that routes around remembered enemy defenses, computed from a threat field weighted by defense type (Pillbox/Turret/Tesla high; AA low). It is ALREADY used in SquadAttackKnownBase (the fog-of-war fallback) for ground and naval, and works.

Gap: visible-enemy attack paths skip the waypoint and go straight to the target.
- SquadAttackMove (ground, in actions.go) → calls sendAttackMove(env, conn, ids, enemy.X, enemy.Y)
- SquadAirStrike (air, in actions.go) → sends Attack(target) directly, no routing
- naval squad-attack also skips it

Fix:
1. Ground: lift the existing ApproachWaypoint check from SquadAttackKnownBase into SquadAttackMove. When squad centroid is far from target AND there's a hot threat corridor, attack-move to waypoint instead of target.
2. Air: add AirThreatField + AirApproachWaypoint that weights AA only (AAGun/SAMSite high; ground defenses zero — they don't shoot aircraft). In SquadAirStrike, when squad far from target AND AA threat in corridor, send Move to waypoint first. Once squad reaches waypoint, fall through to direct Attack on target.
3. Naval: same lift for SquadAttackMove path.

Acceptance: with a clustered SAM/AA wall on one side of an enemy base, vimy aircraft route to the open flank before engaging instead of crossing the SAM cluster. Existing tests cover ApproachWaypoint detection; add a test that SquadAirStrike, given an AA cluster between squad and target, issues Move to a non-cluster zone before issuing Attack.
notes: Game 23 result: changes worked at the squad level (squad-air-attack 26x, squad-attack 230x — engagements happened) but the broader game was lost to a different bug: recall-overextended yanking units back from the enemy base mid-attack (filed as separate bead).
close_reason: Lifted threat-aware approach waypoint into visible-enemy attack paths. (1) SquadAttackMove (ground) now routes via env.ApproachWaypoint when the squad is far from target and the corridor has hot defenses — same logic that already existed for SquadAttackKnownBase, just extracted into groundApproachWaypointFor helper. (2) Added AirThreatField + AirApproachWaypoint in env.go using AA-only weights (AAGun=2.0, SAMSite=2.5, ground defenses ignored). (3) SquadAirStrike now sends AttackMove to the AA-aware waypoint when far from target, only switching to direct Attack once the squad reaches the safer flank. Refactored ApproachWaypoint to share approachWaypointWithField with the air variant. Tests added: TestAirApproachWaypoint_RoutesAroundAA (SAM cluster forces flank), TestAirApproachWaypoint_IgnoresGroundDefenses (pillbox/tesla don't trigger air routing). All existing tests still pass.

title: Add harvester-emergency hard-lock when sustained harvester_under_attack
description:
Game 22 vs russia (lost, 28740 ticks): vimy was rushed — flee-harvesters fired 602x and return-idle-harvesters 322x starting around tick 8800. The 27 doctrines that followed oscillated vehicle 0.55 ↔ infantry 0.6 with ground_def 0.55–0.8 but never cohered into a counter-rush response. Only 4 build-base-defense and 6 place-ready-defense fired the entire match.

IMPORTANT NUANCE (from user observation watching the match): in a rush scenario harvesters will ALWAYS be under attack — small base, no perimeter yet. The naive fix (lock pure defensive: aggression=0, capture=0, ground_def=0.9) is WRONG for this case. The right response to a rush is to kill the attackers fast: rifle/dog spam for body count, pillbox at the threatened side, keep some aggression for counter-pressure. Pure turtle just lets the rusher establish a siege.

The correct fix needs to distinguish two cases and respond differently:

1. RUSH (early game, small base under sustained pressure):
   - Signal: tick < ~6000 AND (multiple harvester_under_attack OR base_under_attack) AND our building count < ~6
   - Response: produce_infantry priority floor, ground_def >= 0.7 (for pillboxes), aggression stays 0.5-0.6 (counter-attack the rushers, don't turtle), capture=0, transport=0, preferred_infantry includes rifleman + (rocket_soldier or attack_dog), no expensive tech detours
   - Key: stay flexible enough to PUSH BACK once the rush is broken

2. RAID HARASSMENT (mid/late game, established economy losing harvesters one-at-a-time):
   - Signal: tick > ~10000 AND repeated harvester_under_attack/lost AND building count > ~10 (established base)
   - Response: escorts near refineries, pillboxes/AA near refineries, can afford to briefly slow the main push but don't abandon it

Computation in agent/strategist.go from stress events + game state, surfaced as TWO separate boolean flags in GameSituation:
- being_rushed bool — drives a RUSH RESPONSE prompt rule
- harvester_harassed bool — drives a softer HARVESTER HARASSMENT rule

Each prompt rule is a hard constraint when its flag is true, but they prescribe different shapes (counter-force vs. dispersal/escort). Both should hold for 2-3 evals after signals clear.

Acceptance: in game 22's situation around tick 9000 (small base, sustained pressure, low building count), being_rushed=true → next doctrine produces rifles/dogs at floor priority + pillbox at threatened side, but keeps aggression high enough to counter-attack rather than turtle. The historical 'keep flipping vehicle/infantry without commitment' pattern goes away because the rule pins the response shape.
notes: User watched game 22 and corrected the framing: harvesters being under attack in a rush is normal, not an emergency. Don't over-index on harvester_under_attack alone — pair it with base size + game phase + base_under_attack to distinguish rush from raid.
close_reason: Added two pressure flags split out from raw harvester_under_attack signal. computePressureFlags() in agent/strategist.go derives being_rushed (tick<6000 + base<=6 buildings + recent harvester pressure) and harvester_harassed (tick>=6000 + base>=8 + 2+ recent harvester events). Surfaced as new GameSituation fields in baml_src/doctrine.baml. Two new prompt rules: RUSH RESPONSE pins infantry>=0.5, ground_def>=0.6, aggression 0.4-0.6 (counter-force, NOT turtle), capture/transport=0, cheap defenders in preferred_infantry. HARVESTER HARASSMENT pins ground_def>=0.7, economy>=0.7, capture<=0.2, allows aggression to stay moderate. Distinct shapes for the two cases. Tests in agent/strategist_test.go cover rush detection, base-growth-clears-rush, harassment with 2+ events, stale-event filtering, and quiet baseline.

title: deliver-apc-to-target never fires despite successful loads
description:
Game 16: load-engineer-into-apc fired 3 times but deliver-apc-to-target 0 times. Either (a) the engineer never completed entering the APC (engineer or APC killed mid-load), (b) the APC stayed in 'moving' state after the load and never went idle, or (c) the apcIntentEngineer marker gets pruned before deliver evaluates.

Needs IPC trace to confirm root cause. Worth investigating whether ActionLoadEngineerIntoAPC's TypeEnterTransport command leaves the APC in a non-idle state until completion.

title: LLM repeatedly tries air pivots despite weak ratings on prior air doctrines this game
description:
Game 15: 'Air Supremacy Pivot — SEAD & Strike' rated weak. Then 'Air-Pivot with AA Suppression' rated weak. Then more air pivots later in the game. The librarian is rating air pivots weak in real time but the LLM keeps reaching for them anyway because lessons-from-this-game aren't fed back into the prompt; only cross-game lessons are surfaced via memory.

Fix direction: surface live in-game doctrine ratings to the LLM in recent_doctrines, OR add a 'tried-and-failed-this-game' axes list (e.g., 'air pivot rated weak at tick X'). Once an axis is rated weak twice in this game, the LLM should refuse to re-pivot to it for the rest of the match.
close_reason: Added BURNED AXIS rule to doctrine.baml prompt: 2+ pivots to the same dominant axis, each followed by domain-specific counter signals (air→aircraft losses, vehicle→army_devastated, infantry→pillbox/flame counters), marks that axis as burned for the rest of the match. LLM must pick a different axis. Live ratings aren't available (only post-game), so this uses the events feed as the proxy.

title: Endgame stall vs coastal naval-yard defended by gunships/destroyers
description:
Observed live: Vimy effectively won but cannot close out an enemy naval yard surrounded by gunships + 2 destroyers. NavalWeight=0 for the whole game so Vimy can't contest naval, V2s lack the range from shore, and aircraft get attrited by AA if the enemy still has any.

Fix options (not yet decided):
1. Auto-enable minimal naval production when remaining enemy assets are all water-sited and we have a naval yard buildable.
2. Superweapon / parabomb / nuke trigger on stubborn last-target clusters.
3. Suicide demo truck / MAD tank push via shore.
4. Detect 'no land targets remain' state and feed as a hint to the strategist so it can pivot naval_weight > 0.

Needs design discussion before coding.
notes:
Map context: enemy naval yard is in a LANDLOCKED lake inaccessible to our navy. Option 1 (auto-enable naval) is moot. Real options are:
1. Aircraft focus-fire on the naval yard once enemy AA is broken.
2. Parabomb / nuke targeting the cluster.
3. V2/artillery from the nearest shore if within range.
4. Detect 'all remaining enemy structures are unreachable by ground' and trigger aircraft/superweapon close-out focus.

Likely the cleanest long-term fix: endgame-closer rule that, when no reachable-by-ground enemy targets remain but enemy structures still exist, promotes aircraft and superweapon fires to target those specific structures.

title: Add combined-arms-countered adaptation rule to doctrine prompt
description: 3-hour stalemate: turtle France opponent clustered AA (sam/agun) adjacent to ground defenses (pbox/gun/tsla). Vimy's air got shot down closing on AA, ground got killed closing on pbox. The doctrine kept respawning 'Air Supremacy with AA Suppression' variants across 5 doctrine generations but had no way to break through because both counters were co-located.\n\nHuman answer: stand off with v2_launcher / artillery that outrange both. The current CRITICAL ADAPTATION RULES cover infantry-vs-static and vehicle-vs-tesla cases but have no rule for the combined-arms-counter case. Added a new adaptation rule naming the symptoms (aircraft losses + ground stall + clustered AA+defenses) and the response (add v2/artillery + raise tech_priority).

title: Scale produce-siege-vehicle cash gate by VehicleWeight (same pattern as vimy-so2)

title: Scale savings reserves by VehicleWeight in produce-vehicle cash gate
description:
When a doctrine explicitly prioritizes vehicles (VehicleWeight >= DoctrineHigh), produce-vehicle's full 800+c.savings cash gate makes tank production infeasible in rush windows — effective threshold can be 3000+ credits when tech-center + advanced-power reserves stack, locking out combat vehicle production entirely for 10+ minutes. title: Base-centroid inference including sighted harvester positions
description:
User asked for an inferred enemy-base center that uses all sightings so far, explicitly including harvesters. Current state: NearestEnemyBase returns a single centroid computed each tick from currently-visible enemy buildings (one per owner); harvester sightings only seed initial intel and otherwise go unused.

Add:
- InferredEnemyBaseCenter() *IntelCenter returning a weighted centroid combining currently-visible enemy buildings (weight 3.0 each), currently-visible enemy harvesters (weight 1.0 each), persistent harvester last-known positions (weight 1.0 each, decayed past 500 ticks), and the persistent high-confidence base intel from enemyBases (weight 5.0 each).
- updateHarvesterIntel called from the engine each tick to persist enemy harvester last-known positions by ID. Harvesters cluster near refineries which sit inside enemy bases — so their positions are useful location intel even when we've lost sight of buildings.

This gives siege/artillery rules a probable-base point even when only fragments have been scouted, and lifts harvester sightings to meaningful intel rather than throwaway.

title: Exclude attack dogs from offensive/emergency ground pools
description:

title: Flak truck dominates vehicle production when tanks are tech-gated
description:
In game id 1, produce-flak-truck fired 15 times and produce-vehicle fired only 3 times across a 38-minute game. User specifically noticed flak trucks were the only vehicles built (besides APCs).

Two compounding factors:
1. produce-vehicle uses BestBuildableVehicle() which round-robins over combatVehicleRoles = [heavy_tank, medium_tank, tesla_tank, light_tank, v2_launcher, artillery, ranger, flak_truck, demo_truck, mad_tank]. When the game hasn't built radar yet (priority 570 after the recent rush-mode fix), heavy/medium/tesla/v2/artillery are all radar-gated, so BestBuildable cascades down the list and ends up returning flak_truck or light_tank. produce-vehicle then queues a flak_truck.
2. produce-flak-truck (priority 470) is also in CatProduceVehicle — so once produce-vehicle hits its cap, flak-truck fills the rest. Net: most vehicle production becomes flak trucks even when the doctrine wants combat armor.

Mitigations:
- Let BestBuildableVehicle skip flak_truck — the dedicated produce-flak-truck rule can handle it based on AirDefensePriority.
- Or: hold produce-vehicle when the only buildable role is flak_truck (prefer waiting for radar rather than producing a non-combat vehicle).

Related to vimy-p0j (rush doctrines losing to air/paratrooper superweapons): if vimy built light_tank or medium_tank instead of flak trucks, it would have more ground pressure to close out games before late-game air threats matured.
notes:
Fixed 2026-09-04. Roles with a dedicated capped rule are excluded from generic
production: `cappedVehicleRoles` = {flak_truck, mad_tank}, applied in both
BestBuildableVehicle and CanBuildAnyCombatVehicle.

Two things the description had slightly wrong, found while applying it:

1. Filtering the fallback alone would not have fixed the reported game. The
   preference list is walked FIRST, and flak_truck was the doctrine's third
   preference — so BestBuildableVehicle landed on it without ever reaching
   combatVehicleRoles. Both paths are filtered now.

2. demo_truck has no dedicated production rule anywhere, in Go or in the .vy
   blocks. Excluding it as the description suggested would have made it
   unbuildable entirely, so it stays in the generic fallback. Only flak_truck
   and mad_tank have rules of their own.

CanBuildAnyCombatVehicle excludes them too, so produce-vehicle holds rather than
firing with nothing worth building. Holding is right now that vimy-tex reserves
cash for radar: the queue waits, the cash accumulates, radar goes up and real
combat vehicles become available. Without vimy-tex this would just have stalled
the Vehicle queue, which is why it blocked this one.

No rule change, so vimyc is untouched — this is entirely in what a predicate
answers.

title: build-extra-refinery gated too high - mid-economy doctrines stuck at 2 refineries
description:
In a 38-minute game (game id 1, current DB), vimy ran with mostly APC/engineer-rush doctrines and only ever built 2 refineries (build-second-refinery fired once, build-extra-refinery never fired). User observed cash banking up mid-game with no refinery expansion.

Root cause: compiler_economy.go:51 only COMPILES build-extra-refinery when EconomyPriority > DoctrineEnabled (0.1) AND refineryMax > 2. refineryMax = lerp(1, 5, EconomyPriority), so refineryMax > 2 requires EconomyPriority > 0.25. But for rush doctrines the LLM often sets EconomyPriority around 0.2-0.3 — right on the edge. When below the threshold the rule doesn't exist, so no amount of banked cash triggers expansion.

Options to consider:
1. Drop the refineryMax > 2 gate and always compile build-extra-refinery with low priority + high cash threshold, so any doctrine banking cash can sink it into more ore production.
2. Keep the compile gate but lower it to DoctrineEnabled (0.1) so only the pure 0 case excludes it.
3. Add a 'cash overflow' emergency rule that builds a refinery whenever Cash() is high enough to cover one with a big buffer, regardless of doctrine weights.

Linked to vimy-p0j (retrospective reliability) and indirectly to the air-def gap — more refineries => more cash => more air defense feasible.

title: Align Go identifier spellings with the vimyc rule language
description: Pass 3 of aligning vimy-core's string identifiers with the kebab vocabulary the vimyc rule language defines. Blocked until vimyc actually emits rule sets, so the change can be tested against a real consumer rather than guessed at.
design:
vimyc (~/code/vimyc) defines its vocabulary as uniformly kebab. It deliberately
holds NO mapping table to Go's spellings — an earlier version derived them and it
was removed, because nothing emits yet and it made the language carry a
consumer's historical inconsistency. Reasoning is in vimyc/docs/design.md under
"Go adapts to the language, not the reverse".

DONE (pass 1, this commit):
  - 12 category values snake -> kebab (squad_form, air_combat, naval_combat,
    emergency_defense, ground_attack_choice, superweapon_build,
    vehicle_maintenance, aircraft_maintenance, and the four Cat* production
    constants). Not persisted anywhere; 2 test assertions updated.
  - 56 ActionRegistry keys snake -> kebab. Note the map is declared and never
    read anywhere in the repo.
  - Squad names were already kebab.

REMAINING (this issue):
  - Roles (52, roles.go): war_factory, rocket_soldier, ... These are the hard
    ones and were deliberately skipped. They are entangled well beyond the rule
    engine:
      * persisted in archived_doctrines.doctrine_json as preferred_infantry /
        preferred_vehicle / preferred_aircraft / preferred_naval arrays
      * written by hand into baml_src/doctrine.baml prompt text AND few-shot
        examples
      * fed back to the LLM by QueryExemplarDoctrines, so old exemplars would
        carry the old spelling while new prompts taught the new one
    Renaming needs a doctrine_json migration plus a prompt rewrite, or a
    compatibility shim that reads both.

  - Predicate names: RuleEnv methods are PascalCase because they are exported Go
    identifiers. vimyc spells them kebab (can-build-role -> CanBuildRole). This
    is mechanical and needs no Go change, just a conversion at the emit boundary.

NOT IN SCOPE, EVER:
  - OpenRA actor and queue names (powr, e1, proc, weap, Building, Infantry).
    Not Vimy's to rename.

ALSO WORTH DECIDING:
  ActionRegistry has no consumers. Either the vimyc `do` field becomes its
  consumer, or the map should be deleted rather than maintained.
acceptance_criteria: vimyc emits a rule set that vimy-core loads without any name translation, or with translation confined to one documented function at the emit boundary. Existing doctrine_json history still resolves.

title: Forfeit/surrender when economy collapsed and no recovery possible
description:
Game 22 vs russia: last unit production fired at tick 9500, last building at tick 13530, but match continued to tick 28740 (15000+ ticks of dead time). During that window the strategist generated ~10 more doctrines and made ~10 more LLM calls — all useless, since no production was happening. This also pollutes retros with late-game doctrines that look 'adequate' on paper but had zero effect.

Proposed: detect economy-collapse state in the agent loop — (harvester_count == 0 AND cash < 200 AND no production fired for last N ticks) → either:
  a) issue a Surrender command via IPC and end the match cleanly, OR
  b) stop calling the LLM strategist (skip evaluations) and just let the bot run on the last doctrine until killed, so we don't burn API credits or pollute the doctrine history.

Option (b) is cheaper to implement and probably enough. Option (a) requires checking whether OpenRA exposes a Surrender bot command.

Acceptance: in game 22's trajectory, no new archived_doctrines rows after the last successful build/produce action's tick + ~2000 ticks.

title: Capture pipeline can't reach water-isolated capturables (island bio labs, etc.)
description:
Live observation: a bio lab in the middle of the map is on an island. The current capture pipeline (produce-engineer → produce-apc/ranger → load → deliver-apc-to-target → capture) is entirely ground-based. APC and Ranger don't cross water, IdleEmptyAPCs only matches apc/ranger types, and there's no rule for amphibious transport (LST/hovercraft in OpenRA RA). Result: an island-locked capturable is structurally unreachable by engineers regardless of capture_priority.

Bumping bio's value (currently 4 in capturableValue) without addressing this just makes the LLM produce engineers that sit at the shore.

Scope of a real fix:
1. Detect water between engineer and capturable (or 'capturable on a different landmass than our base').
2. Route via amphibious transport — LST exists in RA; needs a new role mapping, production rule, load action, sea-crossing action, and a deliver/unload-on-shore action.
3. OR fall back: paratrooper + engineer drop (if airfield), chronoshift for Allies.
4. Smaller intermediate fix: filter capturables by reachability so capture rules don't fire on unreachable targets — at least stops engineer/APC waste.

Filed as feature for later — defer until current core stability work settles.

value: Game 107 (germany vs ukraine, 50700 ticks, loss) is the longest game of the run and validated the f72f530 retune of the infantry-reserves escape. Peak combat vehicles reached exactly 4, the new threshold, so the hold released for the first time; infantry recovered 18 -> 30 and armour held at 5, total fielded 23 -> 35. Defences 9/8 and economy 5 refineries / 7 harvesters, both best-equal. Armour did NOT recover to the 9 of the game 105 win, and medium tanks peaked at 3 rather than 5 — armour is now cash-bound, with produce-vehicle needing 800 against a cash median of 366. Economy is the next ceiling: 5/7 is the best Vimy has managed and still funds only 4-5 live vehicles.

Vimy won its first game on 2026-09-11: game 105, germany vs russia, 37070 ticks, after 104 losses. The win followed five changes made that day: the service-depot savings clause (vimy-2kx), the scout fixes (vimy-xhz), the production-cap overhaul plus the force_size doctrine param (vimy-ogl), and the infantry-reserves fix that stopped rifles outbidding armour (vimy-tbe). Force at the win: 5 medium tanks, 4 artillery, 31 rifles, 9 defences. n=1 — games 98 and 99 were also against russia and were losses at ~30700 ticks.

Export states carry no tick. Never map state index to tick by uniform fraction of duration — sampling is every 15th EVALUATION, not every N ticks, so a degenerate game (e.g. post-CY-loss) over-samples and skews any segment analysis. Build the map from cases[]: firstTick[c.state]=c.tick, as currie/replay.go:205 does. Mapping game 100 uniformly produced a false 'defences unbuildable 59% of opening' that vanished (87%) under the real mapping.

Database work in this project uses sqlc for query generation + goose for migrations. sqlc reads the goose migrations directory as its schema source (one source of truth). Generation step belongs in vimy-core/Makefile 'generate' target alongside baml-cli generate. Pure-Go SQLite driver modernc.org/sqlite (no cgo).
